tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# Readiness Gate

Before generating any tracking, judge whether the plan can actually be built. If the user only asked to check readiness, this gate is the deliverable — report the verdict and stop.

Inventory what planning actually exists: scan `{planning_artifacts}` and `{project_knowledge}` for intent and planning artifacts — briefs, PRFAQs, PRDs, specs, UX outputs, architecture, epics and stories. Identify documents by reading what they are, not by filename patterns; projects arrive with different artifact mixes and naming.

Assess the plan as a whole against one question: **could a developer implement these epics without inventing decisions nothing records?**

- Requirements and decisions in the intent artifacts trace forward into stories; stories trace back to recorded intent — flag orphans in both directions
- Epics deliver user value and carry no forward dependencies; stories are independently completable
- Architecture and UX decisions the stories rely on are recorded somewhere, not assumed
- Conflicts between artifacts (a spec and an epic disagreeing) are surfaced, not silently resolved

A missing document type is only a finding if stories depend on decisions nothing records — a project with no UX artifact and no UI stories is fine.

Deliver a verdict:

- **PASS** — state it in one line; for the full sprint-planning intent, continue with `generate-tracking.md`
- **CONCERNS** — list them briefly with where each gap lives; ask `{user_name}` whether to proceed anyway or fix first
- **FAIL** — the plan is not implementable as recorded. Present findings ordered by severity, name the skill that fixes each (the relevant plan skill, or `bmad-correct-course` for cross-cutting changes), offer to save the findings to `{planning_artifacts}/implementation-readiness.md`, and stop

10	# Cerne - Epic Breakdown
11	
12	## Overview
13	
14	This document provides the complete epic and story breakdown for Cerne, decomposing the requirements from the PRD, UX Design contract, and Architecture Spine into implementable stories.
15	
16	## Requirements Inventory
17	
18	### Functional Requirements
19	
20	**4.1 Foundation & Session Management (F000)**
21	
22	- FR-1: Account creation and authentication — signup, login, silent refresh/session-check, all round-tripping through the backend and surfacing the Failure contract on error; a valid session persists across app restarts without re-prompting. `[ASSUMPTION]` signup collects email + password only (PRD OQ-2).
23	- FR-2: Expired-session recovery overlay — a "Sessão expirada" overlay appears over the current screen (never navigates away) when the backend reports an expired session; "Entrar novamente" routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow (RF03), not a login form; screen state/scroll position preserved underneath.
24	- FR-3: Base navigation shell — navigation between Home/Chat, side menu, Meus Registros, and Configurações reachable from launch, with visually distinguishable placeholders for not-yet-built RF01–RF10 functionality.
25	
26	**4.2 Biometric Authentication Vault (RF03)**
27	
28	- FR-4: App-access gate — Face ID/Touch ID/PIN required before any user data is shown, on cold start and after the idle timeout (FR-6); no biometric data or call ever reaches the backend.
29	- FR-5: Biometric-failure fallback to PIN — a failed biometric attempt always offers a reachable PIN path; never locks the user out; an OS-level lockout is detected and routed to the app's own PIN fallback.
30	- FR-6: Fixed idle re-authentication timeout — 5 minutes backgrounded triggers re-auth on resume; fixed, not user-configurable.
31	- FR-7: Biometric preference persistence — enable/disable biometric gating is saved via `PATCH /account/settings`, survives restarts and reinstalls (fetched from account, not cached locally only); disabling biometrics still leaves PIN as the access method.
32	
33	**4.3 Multimodal Capture (RF01)**
34	
35	- FR-8: Text Entry capture — free text typed in the Insertion Modal saved as an Entry (`source=manual`).
36	- FR-9: Audio Entry capture — audio recorded in the Insertion Modal becomes the basis of an Entry (`source=audio`) once processed (RF02).
37	- FR-10: Photo Entry capture — a captured/selected photo becomes the basis of an Entry (`source=photo`) once processed (RF02). *(FR-8–10 consequence: all three modalities produce the same persisted Entry shape; each `POST /entries` call carries the correct `source`.)*
38	- FR-11: Cancel-safe capture — interrupting a capture in progress (stop before saving, back out mid-photo) never creates a partial/empty Entry; no `POST /entries` call fires for an abandoned capture. `[OPEN]` tab-switch mid-capture behavior (PRD OQ-3) — resolved by UX-DR25 below: cancels the in-flight capture outright.
39	
40	**4.4 Speech-to-Text / OCR Processing (RF02)**
41	
42	- FR-12: On-device audio transcription — audio is transcribed to text entirely on-device via `whisper_ggml`; the audio file itself is never sent to the backend. Four states in sequence: recording → processing → transcribed → (on failure) error with retry, media never discarded.
43	- FR-13: Backend OCR for photos — a captured photo is sent to `POST /media/ocr` to extract text before the Entry is created. Mirrors FR-12's four-state pattern; on failure, two recovery paths exist (retry OCR, or "Salvar só a foto" with no extracted text); `OCR_NO_TEXT` is a distinct, user-visible, non-retryable outcome.
44	
45	**4.5 Multi-Source History / Timeline (RF07)**
46	
47	- FR-14: Chronological Entry list — all Entries from any source listed together, grouped by date, each visually marked with its origin.
48	- FR-15: Per-entry Sync Badge — one of three states (Synchronizing / Synchronization error / Synchronized), derived client-side from `updatedAt`/`serverRevision` plus local pending-write state; the badge stream is independent of the auth/session stream. `[OPEN]` no retry affordance visible in the prototype (PRD OQ-6) — resolved by UX-DR30 below.
49	- FR-16: Empty-state handling — zero Entries shows a dedicated empty state with a path back to capture, not a blank list.
50	- FR-17: Session-expiry resilience mid-view — the FR-2 overlay appears over the timeline without crashing or losing scroll position.
51	- FR-18: Entry detail view — a single Entry can be opened from the timeline via `GET /entries/:id`; never mutates it (no edit affordance); a detail request for another user's/nonexistent Entry returns `NOT_FOUND` (RNF04). *Feature-specific NFR: no BLoC in this feature imports another BLoC directly — the auth-status, Sync-Badge-state, and Entry-data streams combine only through the domain layer.*
52	
53	**4.6 Semantic Search / Filter (RF06)**
54	
55	- FR-19: Semantic search — meaning-based search over Entries (not literal keyword match) via `GET /entries/search`.
56	- FR-20: Metadata filters — filter by source and date range (`dateFrom`/`dateTo`), no tag/category filter; no-search-term filtering queries `GET /entries`, filtering + active search term queries `GET /entries/search` with the same filter params. *(FR-19/20 consequence: multiple active filters combine with AND semantics.)* `[OPEN]` search+filter interaction (PRD OQ-7) — resolved by UX-DR29 below: AND-combine against `GET /entries/search`.
57	- FR-21: Debounced search input — 300ms debounce before firing a request.
58	- FR-22: Non-disruptive filter clearing — clearing filters restores the full list in place (no full reload); cache stays duplicate-free after a reconnect (cloud-only; offline is view-only here).
59	
60	**4.7 Interactive Chat with Memory / RAG (RF04)**
61	
62	- FR-23: Send message, receive RAG-grounded streaming response — via SSE on `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`; exactly three visible states (streaming/processing, error, complete); Chat Messages never automatically create Entries (RF10 is the sole exception).
63	- FR-24: Multi-session chat history — multiple named Chat Sessions, listed and switchable from the side menu.
64	- FR-25: New-conversation action — start a new Chat Session from the side menu; `POST /chat/sessions` is blocked offline.
65	- FR-26: Dropped-stream resilience — if a response stream drops mid-generation, the partial message stays on screen with a failure indicator; retryable via `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` without duplicating the original question.
66	- FR-27: Offline composer lock — composer disabled while offline; existing conversation history stays visible and navigable.
67	
68	**4.8 Save Chat Message as Entry (RF10)** — depends on RF01, RF04
69	
70	- FR-28: Bookmark a user message into an Entry — a "save" affordance on the user's own Chat Messages only (never AI responses) creates an Entry (`source=chat`, carrying `chatMessageId`) through the same shared entries use case RF01 defines, never by importing the entries repository/data source directly (RNF06).
71	- FR-29: Idempotent save — saving the same Chat Message more than once never creates a duplicate Entry and never surfaces a conflict error (backend returns 200, not 409).
72	- FR-30: Save-failure isolation — on save failure, the surrounding Chat Session stays fully usable; the save affordance resets to a retryable state rather than freezing.
73	
74	**4.9 Proactive Insights (RF08)** — depends on RF04; scope is trigger/injection mechanism only, generated-text quality out of scope
75	
76	- FR-31: Unprompted Insight injection — injected into the active Chat Session once per satisfied condition (5 user messages OR 2 minutes inactivity, whichever first) via `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight`.
77	- FR-32: Insight failure isolation — a failed Insight generation never interrupts or breaks the main chat experience; composer stays enabled, no error overlay, ordinary chat messages keep working.
78	- FR-33: Non-disruptive dismissal — dismissing an Insight never affects scroll position or other conversation state.
79	
80	**4.10 Personal Summary Export (RF05)** — depends on RF07; scope is job/file/failure handling only, generated-narrative quality out of scope
81	
82	- FR-34: Request a period export — via `POST /export/summary` for a chosen date period.
83	- FR-35: Job status across five screen states — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio — via `GET /export/:jobId/status`, reporting `status` (job) and `narrativeStatus` (AI summary) independently.
84	- FR-36: Narrative-independent raw-data download — raw data downloadable via `GET /export/:jobId/download` as soon as ready, even if the narrative step is still processing, failed, or skipped; the narrative never blocks the download.
85	- FR-37: Empty-period handling — an export request for a period with zero Entries surfaces "Período vazio," no download offered, no crash.
86	
87	**4.11 Temporal Summaries / Dashboard & Account (RF09)** — depends on F000, RF01; Dashboard scope is aggregation/rendering only, narrative-text quality out of scope
88	
89	- FR-38: On-demand dashboard aggregation — opening Configurações computes/renders an evolution chart via `GET /dashboard/aggregate`, correctly at zero, one, and >30 Entries.
90	- FR-39: Independent narrative text — fetched via `GET /dashboard/narrative`; its failure is a distinct, chart-still-renders state, never blocking the chart (two independent endpoints by design).
91	- FR-40: Cache invalidation on new Entry — dashboard aggregation recalculates after a new Entry is created elsewhere in the app; invalidation only ever triggers on create (Entries are immutable, never edited).
92	- FR-41: Profile name editing — inline display-name edit on Configurações via `PATCH /account/settings`.
93	- FR-42: Logout — "Sair" ends the session (`POST /auth/logout`) and returns to the Biometric Vault / login screen.
94	- FR-43: Account deletion — "Apagar conta" shows a confirmation dialog; on confirm, account and all data are hard-deleted (`DELETE /account`, LGPD-driven); routes to the same destination as logout. `[NOTE]` no dedicated "account deleted" confirmation screen exists (PRD OQ-4).
95	
96	### NonFunctional Requirements
97	
98	- RNF01 (performance): local UI interactions respond in <100ms; any network call taking >300ms shows a loading indicator. Verified by manual timing spot-check per feature module (no automated perf instrumentation planned).
99	- RNF02 (PII handling) `[inherited, not verified by this delivery]`: PII stripping runs server-side via a Claude Haiku 4.5 structured prompt/tool-use step.
100	- RNF03 (data retention) `[inherited, not verified by this delivery]`: zero data retention by upstream AI providers.
101	- RNF04 (data isolation): Row Level Security (Supabase) enforces per-user data isolation; client never needs its own cross-user authorization logic; the backend uniformly returns `NOT_FOUND` (never permission-denied) for another user's resource.
102	- RNF05 (account deletion): hard delete of account and all associated data on request (LGPD).
103	- RNF06 (architecture): zero Clean Architecture layer violations — the domain layer imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything from a `data/` layer, across all 11 feature modules.
104	- RNF07 (test coverage): ≥80% domain-layer test coverage.
105	- RNF08 (visual fidelity): visual fidelity to the prototype (color, typography, spacing); zero hardcoded visual values outside `design_tokens.dart`.
106	- RNF09 (resilience): every repository returns `Either<Failure, T>`; 5 write endpoints × 3 failure types (timeout, malformed response, no connection) = 15 tested failure scenarios, zero unhandled exceptions.
107	
108	### Additional Requirements

112	- Delivery order governs epic/story sequencing: F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09 — later units assume earlier ones exist (e.g., RF10 assumes RF01 and RF04 are both done). No reordering.

115	- AD-2 (binds: all repositories) — every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` for the chat SSE stream); no native/dio exception escapes unmapped.
116	- AD-3 (binds: all) — one sealed `Failure` class in `core/`, exactly 14 subtypes (13 from `error-taxonomy.md` + local-only `MalformedResponse`); never redefined or subset per feature; `AuthInvalid` only ever originates from `POST /auth/login`.

360	As a returning user,
361	I want my session refreshed silently or remembered across app restarts,
362	So that I don't have to log in every time I open the app.
363	
364	**Acceptance Criteria:**
365	
366	**Given** a previously authenticated session with a valid, unexpired token
367	**When** I restart the app
368	**Then** I land on Home/Chat without being re-prompted for credentials.
369	
370	**Given** a session nearing or past expiry on app foreground
371	**When** the app checks session validity
372	**Then** it calls the session-check/refresh operation silently, with no visible loading UI unless the call exceeds the 300ms threshold (RNF01).
373	**And** exactly one `SessionStatus` stream is exposed from `features/auth/domain/` and registered once in DI as a singleton (AD-8) — no other code path re-derives session validity from a raw 401 or a second stream.
374	
375	### Story 1.5: Expired-Session Recovery Overlay
376	
377	As a user whose session has expired while using the app,
378	I want a "Sessão expirada" overlay that lets me re-authenticate without losing my place,
379	So that I never lose my context or feel like I'm starting over.
380	
381	**Acceptance Criteria:**
382	
383	**Given** I am on any screen and the backend reports `AUTH_EXPIRED`
384	**When** the overlay appears
385	**Then** it renders as a scrim over the current screen (confirmation-dialog component, neutral `colorTextPrimary` title, UX-DR16) — the screen underneath, including scroll position, is preserved, never navigated away from.
386	
387	**Given** the overlay is visible
388	**When** I tap "Entrar novamente"
389	**Then** I am routed to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow (built in Epic 2) — never a full login form.
390	
391	**Given** the overlay is open
392	**When** I try to interact with anything underneath the scrim
393	**Then** focus is trapped on the overlay until it is dismissed or actioned (UX-DR25).
394	**And** its entrance uses only the `scrimIn` (0.18s) choreography, and it is the only overlay permitted on screen at a time — it never stacks on top of another open overlay (UX-DR27, UX-DR36).
395	
396	### Story 1.6: Base Navigation Shell with Feature Placeholders
397	
398	As a user,
399	I want to navigate between Home/Chat, the side menu, Meus Registros, and Configurações from the moment I open the app,
400	So that the whole app feels complete and navigable even while individual features are still being built.
401	
402	**Acceptance Criteria:**
403	
404	**Given** the app has launched
405	**When** I open the side menu (☰)
406	**Then** I can reach Chat Session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, and Planos de Ação — all four destinations resolve to a screen, none 404s or crashes.
407	
408	**Given** a destination whose RF unit is not yet built
409	**When** I navigate to it
410	**Then** it renders a visually distinct, clearly-marked placeholder — never a screen that looks finished but does nothing.
411	
412	**Given** the Planos de Ação placeholder (an explicit extension feature, never implemented per project policy)
413	**When** I open it
414	**Then** it is styled with full visual polish per the design tokens — never grayed-out or visibly "unfinished" (UX-DR32) — with no backend calls and no interactive drag/drop logic behind it.
415	**And** the side-menu avatar component (solid `colorPrimary` circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, 40px) is implemented here for reuse — not reimplementation — when Configurações needs its 52px variant later (UX-DR13).
416	
417	## Epic 2: Biometric Authentication Vault
418	
419	Users unlock the app with Face ID/Touch ID (or PIN fallback) before any personal data is ever shown, with no lockout path and no biometric data ever leaving the device.
420	
421	### Story 2.1: Biometric/PIN App-Access Gate
422	
423	As a user,
424	I want the app to require Face ID, Touch ID, or PIN before showing any of my data,
425	So that my journal stays private even if someone else picks up my phone.
426	
427	**Acceptance Criteria:**
428	
429	**Given** the app is cold-started or resumed after the idle timeout
430	**When** the vault gate evaluates
431	**Then** no screen other than the vault/login screen is reachable until authentication succeeds.
432	
433	**Given** the `go_router` redirect
434	**When** it evaluates on any navigation attempt
435	**Then** it composes exactly two gates in fixed order — `VaultStatus` first, then `SessionStatus` (AD-14) — and neither gate ever makes a network call to validate itself; biometric validation is 100% on-device, so no biometric data or call ever reaches the backend.
436	
437	**Given** Face ID/Touch ID is available and enabled
438	**When** I open the app
439	**Then** the OS biometric prompt appears and, on success, routes me straight to Home/Chat.
440	**And** `features/vault/domain` exposes a `VaultStatus` stream the same way `features/auth/domain` exposes `SessionStatus` (AD-8 pattern), registered once in DI.
441	
442	### Story 2.2: Biometric-Failure Fallback to PIN
443	
444	As a user whose biometric check fails,
445	I want to fall back to entering a PIN,
446	So that I'm never locked out of my own journal.
447	
448	**Acceptance Criteria:**
449	
450	**Given** Face ID/Touch ID fails to recognize me
451	**When** the failure is reported
452	**Then** "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN" appears with a PIN entry path always reachable — never a dead end.
453	
454	**Given** repeated biometric failures trigger an OS-level lockout
455	**When** that lockout is detected
456	**Then** the app routes to its own PIN fallback rather than retrying against the OS.
457	
458	**Given** the PIN keypad (3×4 grid + backspace, progress dots, structural palette only, UX-DR14)
459	**When** I enter the 4th digit
460	**Then** the app auto-advances 350ms later with no explicit "confirm" tap (UX-DR27).
461	**And** the screen-reader announces the failure transition per the Accessibility Floor (UX-DR21), and the keypad's digits remain legible at the largest Dynamic Type size without truncation (UX-DR22).
462	
463	### Story 2.3: Fixed 5-Minute Idle Re-Authentication Timeout
464	
465	As a user,
466	I want re-authentication required only after 5 minutes backgrounded,
467	So that casual app-switching doesn't interrupt me but a forgotten unlocked phone stays protected.
468	
469	**Acceptance Criteria:**
470	
471	**Given** the app is backgrounded for less than 5 minutes
472	**When** I resume it
473	**Then** no re-authentication is prompted.
474	
475	**Given** the app is backgrounded for 5 minutes or more
476	**When** I resume it
477	**Then** re-authentication is always prompted, regardless of any user setting — this value is fixed, not user-configurable.
478	**And** this timeout is implemented as a fixed parameter within `features/vault/domain`, not as a shared `core/` constant, and is never re-tuned by any later story.
479	
480	### Story 2.4: Biometric Preference Persistence
481	
482	As a user,
483	I want to enable or disable the biometric gate from a setting that persists across restarts and reinstalls,
484	So that my preference travels with my account, not just my device.
485	
486	**Acceptance Criteria:**
487	
488	**Given** I toggle biometric gating on or off
489	**When** the toggle is changed
490	**Then** `PATCH /account/settings` persists the preference server-side, surfacing the Failure contract on error.
491	
492	**Given** I disable biometrics
493	**When** I next open the app
494	**Then** PIN remains available as the access method — the vault itself can never be turned off entirely.
495	
496	**Given** I reinstall the app or restart it after changing this setting elsewhere
497	**When** the app loads
498	**Then** the preference is fetched from the account, not read from a stale local-only cache.
499	**And** this story introduces a minimal Configurações screen (replacing Epic 1's placeholder) containing only this toggle — Epic 8 extends this same screen with profile editing, the dashboard, and account actions; it is never recreated from scratch.
500	
501	## Epic 3: Multimodal Capture & Processing
502	
503	Users can capture a journal Entry as text, voice, or photo — with audio transcribed on-device and photos OCR'd server-side before the Entry is ever persisted — and interrupting a capture never leaves a stray partial Entry behind.
504	
505	### Story 3.1: Text Entry Capture & Insertion Modal Shell
506	
507	As a user,
508	I want to open the "+" control and type free text to save as a journal Entry,
509	So that I can quickly capture what happened today in writing.
510	
511	**Acceptance Criteria:**
512	
513	**Given** I tap "+" on Home/Chat
514	**When** the Insertion Modal opens
515	**Then** it opens on the Texto tab by default with a three-segment tab bar (Texto/Áudio/Foto, UX-DR11) and all three tabs reset to idle/empty.
516	
517	**Given** I type text and tap Salvar
518	**When** the save completes
519	**Then** `POST /entries` fires with `source=manual` and the modal closes, returning me to where I was.
520	
521	**Given** `features/entries/` does not yet exist
522	**When** this story is built
523	**Then** it introduces `entries/domain` owning the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port (`create`), and the entries Hive box (AD-6) — this story is the first consumer of that port, never building its own local Entry model.
524	
525	**Given** the device is offline
526	**When** I tap "+"
527	**Then** the entry point is disabled with the same offline-banner treatment as chat send (UX-DR30, AD-9) — there is no local-only queued write.
528	**And** interrupting before Salvar (closing the modal, switching tabs) never fires `POST /entries` (FR-11 — see Story 3.4 for the full cross-tab rule).
529	
530	### Story 3.2: Audio Entry Capture & On-Device Transcription
531	
532	As a user,
533	I want to record audio in the Insertion Modal and have it transcribed on-device,
534	So that I can speak my day instead of typing it, without my voice ever leaving my phone.
535	
536	**Acceptance Criteria:**
537	
538	**Given** the Áudio tab
539	**When** I start recording
540	**Then** an animated waveform (UX-DR12) shows in the structural palette with a mono counter ticking up.
541	
542	**Given** I stop recording
543	**When** `whisper_ggml` transcribes on-device
544	**Then** the waveform freezes at 35% opacity (UX-DR12) and exactly four states occur in sequence: recording → processing → transcribed → (on failure) error with retry — media is never discarded on failure.
545	
546	**Given** transcription completes
547	**When** I review the text
548	**Then** it is editable before I tap Salvar, and the resulting Entry carries `source=audio`.
549	
550	**Given** the audio file at any point in this pipeline
551	**When** any network call is inspected
552	**Then** no call ever contains audio bytes — transcription is 100% on-device (FR-12).
553	**And** the screen-reader announces each transition ("Gravando," "Transcrevendo," "Erro ao transcrever, toque para tentar novamente") per UX-DR21.
554	
555	### Story 3.3: Photo Entry Capture & Backend OCR
556	
557	As a user,
558	I want to capture or select a photo in the Insertion Modal and have its text recognized,
559	So that I can save a physical note or receipt-like artifact without retyping it.
560	
561	**Acceptance Criteria:**
562	
563	**Given** the Foto tab
564	**When** I capture or select a photo
565	**Then** it is sent to `POST /media/ocr` to extract text before the Entry is created, mirroring the audio pipeline's four-state pattern (capture → processing OCR → recognized → error).
566	
567	**Given** OCR fails with `OCR_NO_TEXT`
568	**When** the error state shows
569	**Then** it is presented as a distinct, non-retryable outcome with two recovery paths — "Tentar novamente" (re-invokes OCR on the same photo) and "Salvar só a foto" (saves the record with no extracted text) — never a single generic failure.
570	
571	**Given** recognized text
572	**When** I review it
573	**Then** it is editable before I tap Salvar, and the resulting Entry carries `source=photo`.
574	
575	**Given** the photo exceeds the upload size limit
576	**When** `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (413, non-retryable) is returned
577	**Then** a size-specific error message is shown with no retry button, since retrying the same oversized file cannot succeed.
578	
579	### Story 3.4: Cancel-Safe Capture Across All Tabs
580	
581	As a user,
582	I want interrupting a capture in progress to never create a partial Entry,
583	So that I never end up with junk in my journal from a capture I abandoned.
584	
585	**Acceptance Criteria:**
586	
587	**Given** a recording or OCR/transcription in progress
588	**When** I switch to a different Insertion Modal tab
589	**Then** the in-flight capture is canceled outright — no partial Entry is created (resolves PRD OQ-3).
590	
591	**Given** I back out of the modal mid-photo or stop a recording before tapping Salvar
592	**When** the modal closes
593	**Then** no `POST /entries` call fires for the abandoned capture.
594	
595	**Given** any of the three tabs
596	**When** a capture is interrupted
597	**Then** it is the Insertion Modal's own internal tab state that resets — the three tabs remain internal states of one sheet, never nested sheets (UX-DR36).
598	
599	## Epic 4: Timeline & History
600	
601	Users can see every Entry they've ever captured, from any source, in one chronological view with a live per-entry sync status — and never lose track of something they wrote, even offline or mid-session-expiry.
602	
603	### Story 4.1: Chronological Entry List with Origin Marking
604	
605	As a user,
606	I want to see every Entry I've ever captured, from any source, in one chronological list grouped by date,
607	So that I never lose track of something I wrote.
608	
609	**Acceptance Criteria:**
610	
611	**Given** Entries from manual, audio, and photo sources
612	**When** Meus Registros loads
613	**Then** all Entries are listed together grouped by date, each visually marked with its origin via the record card's spine color (manual=`colorPrimary`, audio=olive green, photo=gray — chat=`colorAccent` reserved for Epic 6, UX-DR18).
614	
615	**Given** the list is loading
616	**When** the `GET /entries` call takes longer than 300ms
617	**Then** skeleton rows show (UX-DR17); under 300ms, no loading UI appears at all (RNF01).
618	
619	**Given** the session expires while I'm viewing this screen
620	**When** the FR-2 overlay (built in Epic 1) appears
621	**Then** it does so without crashing or losing my scroll position (FR-17).
622	
623	**Given** the entries Hive box
624	**When** Entries are cached locally
625	**Then** it stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id — no local filtering, joining, or sorting of the cached collection (AD-15).
626	**And** no swipe gesture is ever implemented on a record card — Entries are immutable, so no gesture may imply an edit or delete that doesn't exist (UX-DR28).
627	
628	### Story 4.2: Per-Entry Sync Badge
629	
630	As a user,
631	I want to see at a glance whether each Entry has synced,
632	So that I know whether my capture is safely saved.
633	
634	**Acceptance Criteria:**
635	
636	**Given** a freshly created Entry
637	**When** its write is in flight
638	**Then** its badge shows "Synchronizing" (ochre dot) until the server's write confirmation is reconciled, then flips to "Synchronized" (green dot).
639	
640	**Given** a write fails (network or any Failure-contract code)
641	**When** the badge renders
642	**Then** it shows "Synchronization error" (red dot) until a subsequent successful write reconciles it.
643	
644	**Given** the badge is in the error state
645	**When** I tap it
646	**Then** it retries that entry's write if the underlying code is retryable, or shows an inline explanation instead of a retry affordance if it is not (resolves PRD OQ-6).
647	
648	**Given** one derivation function in `entries/domain`
649	**When** any screen renders a sync badge
650	**Then** it consumes that function's output, computed from `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and transient per-entry write state — no screen recomputes the badge inline (AD-10).
651	**And** the badge's dot color is always paired with an accessible label reachable on tap/long-focus, and its tappable retry area is ≥44pt even though the dot itself is small (UX-DR7, UX-DR23) — color never carries the state alone.
652	**And** the badge's update stream runs independently of the auth/session stream — a pending sync-badge transition is never blocked or cleared by session-expiry handling.
653	
654	### Story 4.3: Empty-State Handling
655	
656	As a user with no Entries yet,
657	I want a dedicated empty state instead of a blank list,
658	So that the app guides me back to capture rather than looking broken.
659	
660	**Acceptance Criteria:**
661	
662	**Given** zero Entries exist
663	**When** Meus Registros loads
664	**Then** a dedicated empty state renders — never a blank list.
665	
666	**Given** the empty state
667	**When** I look for a way forward
668	**Then** it offers a path back to capture (a CTA that opens the Insertion Modal).
669	
670	### Story 4.4: Entry Detail View
671	
672	As a user,
673	I want to open a single Entry to see its full content,
674	So that I can review exactly what I wrote without any risk of accidentally changing it.
675	
676	**Acceptance Criteria:**
677	
678	**Given** an Entry in the list
679	**When** I open it
680	**Then** `GET /entries/:id` fetches and displays its full content with no edit affordance anywhere on the screen — Entries are immutable, and `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read only; no update/delete method is ever added (AD-11).
681	
682	**Given** an Entry that doesn't exist or belongs to another user
683	**When** the detail request is made
684	**Then** the backend returns `NOT_FOUND`, never a permission-denied code, and the UI shows the same not-found treatment either way (RNF04).
685	
686	**Given** this screen composes auth status, Sync Badge state, and Entry data
687	**When** those three streams are combined
688	**Then** they combine only through the domain layer — no BLoC in this feature imports another BLoC directly (AD-7, feature-specific NFR).
689	
690	## Epic 5: Semantic Search & Filtering
691	
692	Users can find any Entry again by meaning — not just exact keyword match — and narrow results by source and date range, with search debounced and filters clearing back to the full list without a reload.
693	
694	### Story 5.1: Semantic Search with Debounced Input
695	
696	As a user,
697	I want to search my Entries by meaning, not just exact words,
698	So that I can find things I wrote even if I phrased them differently.
699	
700	**Acceptance Criteria:**
701	
702	**Given** I type "ansiedade" into the search bar
703	**When** results return
704	**Then** they include an Entry that only used a related but different word (e.g., "nervosismo") because the match is semantic (`GET /entries/search`), not literal.
705	
706	**Given** I am typing
707	**When** each keystroke lands
708	**Then** the request is debounced by 300ms before firing — no request fires on every keystroke.
709	
710	**Given** the search bar component (UX-DR9)
711	**When** it renders
712	**Then** it is permanently docked at the top of Meus Registros with a trailing funnel icon and is never submitted with a button.
713	
714	**Given** I am offline
715	**When** I attempt a semantic search
716	**Then** it resolves to `Failure.networkOffline` immediately — there is no client-side vector index to fall back to, so it is never served from cache, unlike plain entry reads (AD-9 search carve-out).
717	
718	### Story 5.2: Metadata Filters
719	
720	As a user,
721	I want to filter my Entries by source and date range,
722	So that I can narrow down to just the Entries I care about.
723	
724	**Acceptance Criteria:**
725	
726	**Given** no active search term
727	**When** I apply a source and/or date-range filter
728	**Then** `GET /entries` is queried with those filter parameters.
729	
730	**Given** multiple active filters
731	**When** they combine
732	**Then** they use AND semantics — no tag/category filter exists, since categorization is an extension feature.
733	
734	**Given** the filter chip component (UX-DR8) and filter sheet (UX-DR10)
735	**When** filters are active
736	**Then** chips render as removable, and the sheet itself is a `radiusLg`/`elevation2` bottom sheet with groups labeled in `textMonoCaption`.
737	
738	### Story 5.3: Combined Search + Filter & Non-Disruptive Clearing
739	
740	As a user,
741	I want my search term and my active filters to work together, and clearing them to feel instant,
742	So that filtering never feels like it's fighting my search.
743	
744	**Acceptance Criteria:**
745	
746	**Given** an active search term and active filters set simultaneously
747	**When** results are requested
748	**Then** `GET /entries/search` is queried carrying the same filter parameters, combined with AND logic (resolves PRD OQ-7, UX-DR29).
749	
750	**Given** active filters
751	**When** I clear them
752	**Then** the full list is restored in place, without a full screen reload.
753	
754	**Given** a reconnect after being offline
755	**When** the cache resyncs
756	**Then** it stays duplicate-free — no Entry appears twice because of a reconnect.
757	
758	## Epic 6: Conversational Memory, Save-to-Journal & Insights
759	
760	Users can have a persistent, multi-session conversation with an assistant that answers grounded in their own past Entries, turn their own reflective messages into real Entries with one tap, and occasionally receive an unprompted insight about a pattern in their writing — none of which ever blocks or corrupts the core chat experience when it fails.
761	
762	### Story 6.1: Send Message & Receive RAG-Grounded Streaming Response
763	
764	As a user,
765	I want to send a message to the assistant and get a response grounded in my own past Entries,
766	So that I feel genuinely understood rather than getting a generic reply.
767	
768	**Acceptance Criteria:**
769	
770	**Given** I type a message referencing something from weeks ago and send it
771	**When** the response streams in via SSE on `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`
772	**Then** it is grounded in semantic retrieval over my own Entries — not a stateless generic answer.
773	
774	**Given** the response is streaming
775	**When** it renders
776	**Then** exactly three visible states exist: streaming/processing (progressively revealed text behind a blinking cursor, chat-bubble component UX-DR4), error, complete.
777	
778	**Given** a Chat Message is sent
779	**When** it completes
780	**Then** it never automatically creates an Entry — RF10 (Story 6.4) is the sole, explicit exception.
781	**And** if Reduce Motion is enabled, the cursor-blink animation is skipped and the final text shows immediately instead (UX-DR24).
782	
783	### Story 6.2: Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation
784	
785	As a user,
786	I want to hold multiple named conversations and start a new one whenever I want a fresh start,
787	So that my chat history stays organized by topic or moment.
788	
789	**Acceptance Criteria:**
790	
791	**Given** I have existing Chat Sessions
792	**When** I open the side menu
793	**Then** they are listed and I can switch between them.
794	
795	**Given** I tap "Novo Chat" from the side menu
796	**When** a new session starts
797	**Then** it opens empty with the composer focused and the placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem..." — no greeting copy invented beyond that.
798	
799	**Given** I am offline
800	**When** I attempt to start a new Chat Session
801	**Then** `POST /chat/sessions` is blocked, consistent with the offline composer lock on existing conversations.
802	**And** a returning (not new) session restores the last conversation's scroll position when I open it.
803	
804	### Story 6.3: Dropped-Stream Resilience & Offline Composer Lock
805	
806	As a user,
807	I want a dropped response or an offline moment to never cost me my place in the conversation,
808	So that a flaky connection never feels like data loss.
809	
810	**Acceptance Criteria:**
811	
812	**Given** a response stream drops mid-generation
813	**When** the failure is detected
814	**Then** the partial message stays on screen with a failure indicator (timestamp slot replaced by red retry copy, bubble content never cleared).
815	
816	**Given** a dropped stream
817	**When** I tap retry
818	**Then** `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` regenerates the response without duplicating my original question.
819

# Cerne - Epic Breakdown

## Overview

This document provides the complete epic and story breakdown for Cerne, decomposing the requirements from the PRD, UX Design contract, and Architecture Spine into implementable stories.

## Requirements Inventory

### Functional Requirements

**4.1 Foundation & Session Management (F000)**

- FR-1: Account creation and authentication — signup, login, silent refresh/session-check, all round-tripping through the backend and surfacing the Failure contract on error; a valid session persists across app restarts without re-prompting. `[ASSUMPTION]` signup collects email + password only (PRD OQ-2).
- FR-2: Expired-session recovery overlay — a "Sessão expirada" overlay appears over the current screen (never navigates away) when the backend reports an expired session; "Entrar novamente" routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow (RF03), not a login form; screen state/scroll position preserved underneath.
- FR-3: Base navigation shell — navigation between Home/Chat, side menu, Meus Registros, and Configurações reachable from launch, with visually distinguishable placeholders for not-yet-built RF01–RF10 functionality.

**4.2 Biometric Authentication Vault (RF03)**

- FR-4: App-access gate — Face ID/Touch ID/PIN required before any user data is shown, on cold start and after the idle timeout (FR-6); no biometric data or call ever reaches the backend.
- FR-5: Biometric-failure fallback to PIN — a failed biometric attempt always offers a reachable PIN path; never locks the user out; an OS-level lockout is detected and routed to the app's own PIN fallback.
- FR-6: Fixed idle re-authentication timeout — 5 minutes backgrounded triggers re-auth on resume; fixed, not user-configurable.
- FR-7: Biometric preference persistence — enable/disable biometric gating is saved via `PATCH /account/settings`, survives restarts and reinstalls (fetched from account, not cached locally only); disabling biometrics still leaves PIN as the access method.

**4.3 Multimodal Capture (RF01)**

- FR-8: Text Entry capture — free text typed in the Insertion Modal saved as an Entry (`source=manual`).
- FR-9: Audio Entry capture — audio recorded in the Insertion Modal becomes the basis of an Entry (`source=audio`) once processed (RF02).
- FR-10: Photo Entry capture — a captured/selected photo becomes the basis of an Entry (`source=photo`) once processed (RF02). *(FR-8–10 consequence: all three modalities produce the same persisted Entry shape; each `POST /entries` call carries the correct `source`.)*
- FR-11: Cancel-safe capture — interrupting a capture in progress (stop before saving, back out mid-photo) never creates a partial/empty Entry; no `POST /entries` call fires for an abandoned capture. `[OPEN]` tab-switch mid-capture behavior (PRD OQ-3) — resolved by UX-DR25 below: cancels the in-flight capture outright.

**4.4 Speech-to-Text / OCR Processing (RF02)**

- FR-12: On-device audio transcription — audio is transcribed to text entirely on-device via `whisper_ggml`; the audio file itself is never sent to the backend. Four states in sequence: recording → processing → transcribed → (on failure) error with retry, media never discarded.
- FR-13: Backend OCR for photos — a captured photo is sent to `POST /media/ocr` to extract text before the Entry is created. Mirrors FR-12's four-state pattern; on failure, two recovery paths exist (retry OCR, or "Salvar só a foto" with no extracted text); `OCR_NO_TEXT` is a distinct, user-visible, non-retryable outcome.

**4.5 Multi-Source History / Timeline (RF07)**

- FR-14: Chronological Entry list — all Entries from any source listed together, grouped by date, each visually marked with its origin.
- FR-15: Per-entry Sync Badge — one of three states (Synchronizing / Synchronization error / Synchronized), derived client-side from `updatedAt`/`serverRevision` plus local pending-write state; the badge stream is independent of the auth/session stream. `[OPEN]` no retry affordance visible in the prototype (PRD OQ-6) — resolved by UX-DR30 below.
- FR-16: Empty-state handling — zero Entries shows a dedicated empty state with a path back to capture, not a blank list.
- FR-17: Session-expiry resilience mid-view — the FR-2 overlay appears over the timeline without crashing or losing scroll position.
- FR-18: Entry detail view — a single Entry can be opened from the timeline via `GET /entries/:id`; never mutates it (no edit affordance); a detail request for another user's/nonexistent Entry returns `NOT_FOUND` (RNF04). *Feature-specific NFR: no BLoC in this feature imports another BLoC directly — the auth-status, Sync-Badge-state, and Entry-data streams combine only through the domain layer.*

**4.6 Semantic Search / Filter (RF06)**

- FR-19: Semantic search — meaning-based search over Entries (not literal keyword match) via `GET /entries/search`.
- FR-20: Metadata filters — filter by source and date range (`dateFrom`/`dateTo`), no tag/category filter; no-search-term filtering queries `GET /entries`, filtering + active search term queries `GET /entries/search` with the same filter params. *(FR-19/20 consequence: multiple active filters combine with AND semantics.)* `[OPEN]` search+filter interaction (PRD OQ-7) — resolved by UX-DR29 below: AND-combine against `GET /entries/search`.
- FR-21: Debounced search input — 300ms debounce before firing a request.
- FR-22: Non-disruptive filter clearing — clearing filters restores the full list in place (no full reload); cache stays duplicate-free after a reconnect (cloud-only; offline is view-only here).

**4.7 Interactive Chat with Memory / RAG (RF04)**

- FR-23: Send message, receive RAG-grounded streaming response — via SSE on `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`; exactly three visible states (streaming/processing, error, complete); Chat Messages never automatically create Entries (RF10 is the sole exception).
- FR-24: Multi-session chat history — multiple named Chat Sessions, listed and switchable from the side menu.
- FR-25: New-conversation action — start a new Chat Session from the side menu; `POST /chat/sessions` is blocked offline.
- FR-26: Dropped-stream resilience — if a response stream drops mid-generation, the partial message stays on screen with a failure indicator; retryable via `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` without duplicating the original question.
- FR-27: Offline composer lock — composer disabled while offline; existing conversation history stays visible and navigable.

**4.8 Save Chat Message as Entry (RF10)** — depends on RF01, RF04

- FR-28: Bookmark a user message into an Entry — a "save" affordance on the user's own Chat Messages only (never AI responses) creates an Entry (`source=chat`, carrying `chatMessageId`) through the same shared entries use case RF01 defines, never by importing the entries repository/data source directly (RNF06).
- FR-29: Idempotent save — saving the same Chat Message more than once never creates a duplicate Entry and never surfaces a conflict error (backend returns 200, not 409).
- FR-30: Save-failure isolation — on save failure, the surrounding Chat Session stays fully usable; the save affordance resets to a retryable state rather than freezing.

**4.9 Proactive Insights (RF08)** — depends on RF04; scope is trigger/injection mechanism only, generated-text quality out of scope

- FR-31: Unprompted Insight injection — injected into the active Chat Session once per satisfied condition (5 user messages OR 2 minutes inactivity, whichever first) via `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight`.
- FR-32: Insight failure isolation — a failed Insight generation never interrupts or breaks the main chat experience; composer stays enabled, no error overlay, ordinary chat messages keep working.
- FR-33: Non-disruptive dismissal — dismissing an Insight never affects scroll position or other conversation state.

**4.10 Personal Summary Export (RF05)** — depends on RF07; scope is job/file/failure handling only, generated-narrative quality out of scope

- FR-34: Request a period export — via `POST /export/summary` for a chosen date period.
- FR-35: Job status across five screen states — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio — via `GET /export/:jobId/status`, reporting `status` (job) and `narrativeStatus` (AI summary) independently.
- FR-36: Narrative-independent raw-data download — raw data downloadable via `GET /export/:jobId/download` as soon as ready, even if the narrative step is still processing, failed, or skipped; the narrative never blocks the download.
- FR-37: Empty-period handling — an export request for a period with zero Entries surfaces "Período vazio," no download offered, no crash.

**4.11 Temporal Summaries / Dashboard & Account (RF09)** — depends on F000, RF01; Dashboard scope is aggregation/rendering only, narrative-text quality out of scope

- FR-38: On-demand dashboard aggregation — opening Configurações computes/renders an evolution chart via `GET /dashboard/aggregate`, correctly at zero, one, and >30 Entries.
- FR-39: Independent narrative text — fetched via `GET /dashboard/narrative`; its failure is a distinct, chart-still-renders state, never blocking the chart (two independent endpoints by design).
- FR-40: Cache invalidation on new Entry — dashboard aggregation recalculates after a new Entry is created elsewhere in the app; invalidation only ever triggers on create (Entries are immutable, never edited).
- FR-41: Profile name editing — inline display-name edit on Configurações via `PATCH /account/settings`.
- FR-42: Logout — "Sair" ends the session (`POST /auth/logout`) and returns to the Biometric Vault / login screen.
- FR-43: Account deletion — "Apagar conta" shows a confirmation dialog; on confirm, account and all data are hard-deleted (`DELETE /account`, LGPD-driven); routes to the same destination as logout. `[NOTE]` no dedicated "account deleted" confirmation screen exists (PRD OQ-4).

### NonFunctional Requirements

- RNF01 (performance): local UI interactions respond in <100ms; any network call taking >300ms shows a loading indicator. Verified by manual timing spot-check per feature module (no automated perf instrumentation planned).
- RNF02 (PII handling) `[inherited, not verified by this delivery]`: PII stripping runs server-side via a Claude Haiku 4.5 structured prompt/tool-use step.
- RNF03 (data retention) `[inherited, not verified by this delivery]`: zero data retention by upstream AI providers.
- RNF04 (data isolation): Row Level Security (Supabase) enforces per-user data isolation; client never needs its own cross-user authorization logic; the backend uniformly returns `NOT_FOUND` (never permission-denied) for another user's resource.
- RNF05 (account deletion): hard delete of account and all associated data on request (LGPD).
- RNF06 (architecture): zero Clean Architecture layer violations — the domain layer imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything from a `data/` layer, across all 11 feature modules.
- RNF07 (test coverage): ≥80% domain-layer test coverage.
- RNF08 (visual fidelity): visual fidelity to the prototype (color, typography, spacing); zero hardcoded visual values outside `design_tokens.dart`.
- RNF09 (resilience): every repository returns `Either<Failure, T>`; 5 write endpoints × 3 failure types (timeout, malformed response, no connection) = 15 tested failure scenarios, zero unhandled exceptions.

### Additional Requirements

*(from the Architecture Spine — cross-unit invariants and stack decisions that bound how stories must be implemented; binds column shows which build units each rule applies to)*

- Delivery order governs epic/story sequencing: F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09 — later units assume earlier ones exist (e.g., RF10 assumes RF01 and RF04 are both done). No reordering.
- **Integration spike required first, inside F000, before any other building:** verify `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` work together in one scaffold bootstrap — flagged as unverified in combination even though each package is independently current.
- AD-1 (binds: all) — strict layer dependency direction `presentation → domain ← data`; only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins; `presentation/` never imports any `data/` directly.
- AD-2 (binds: all repositories) — every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` for the chat SSE stream); no native/dio exception escapes unmapped.
- AD-3 (binds: all) — one sealed `Failure` class in `core/`, exactly 14 subtypes (13 from `error-taxonomy.md` + local-only `MalformedResponse`); never redefined or subset per feature; `AuthInvalid` only ever originates from `POST /auth/login`.
- AD-4 (binds: the API client) — retry logic implemented exactly once (the `dio` interceptor/`ApiClient` wrapper), fires only for the 6 server `retryable:true` codes; every other code surfaces once, unretried.
- AD-5 (binds: every network call) — one URL builder in `core/` maps each operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>`; one `dio` interceptor owns headers (`apikey` always; `Authorization: Bearer <anon key>` only on signup/login/refresh; `Authorization: Bearer <user token>` otherwise).
- AD-6 (binds: RF01 introduces `features/entries/`; RF10 and any future cross-feature dependency consume it) — `entries/domain` owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port, and the Hive box; RF01's `capture` and RF10's `chat` are consumers only (import the abstract port, never `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/`); RF06/RF07 extend the same port with `list`/`search`, never a second entry model; `create` is idempotent on `(origin, chatMessageId)`.
- AD-7 (binds: all) — a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency; composition via injected domain streams/use-cases or `BlocListener`/`MultiBlocListener`.
- AD-8 (binds: F000, RF07, any session-consuming feature) — exactly one `SessionStatus` stream from the auth feature's `domain/`, registered once in DI as a singleton; no consumer re-derives session state from a raw 401 or a second stream.
- AD-9 (binds: all repositories) — a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)`, never queued; plain reads fall back to the local `hive_ce` cache; semantic search (`GET /entries/search`) has no client-side vector index, so it also resolves to `networkOffline` when offline, same as a write.
- AD-10 (binds: every screen rendering the sync badge) — one derivation function in `entries/domain`, computed from `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and transient per-entry write state; every screen consumes that function's output, none recomputes inline.
- AD-11 (binds: the entries feature) — `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read only; no update/delete method is ever added.
- AD-12 (binds: RF06, RF09 — explicitly not RF02/RF04/RF07) — generic `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) in `core/` used only by single-data-source, single-fetch-lifecycle screens; RF02, RF04, and RF07 each define their own sealed state class.
- AD-13 (binds: RF08, RF10) — `core/` holds a never-throws `isolatedSideEffect` helper (`Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped), ships with RF10 (first consumer); RF10 may `await` it, RF08 must call it fire-and-forget (without awaiting).
- AD-14 (binds: F000 builds the redirect skeleton + `SessionStatus` half; RF03 plugs in the vault half) — one `go_router` redirect composing exactly two gates in fixed order: `VaultStatus` first, then `SessionStatus`; neither gate ever reaches the server to validate itself.
- AD-15 (binds: `entries`, `chat` — every feature with a `hive_ce` box) — every query dimension (source, date range, semantic search, pagination cursor) is a server-side query parameter; a Hive box stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id; no feature filters/joins/sorts/re-derives a cached collection locally.
- Stack pins (binding on F000, verified at scaffold time): Flutter SDK 3.47.x stable family (exact patch pinned via `fvm`), `flutter_bloc` ^9.1.1, `go_router` ^18.1.1, `dio` ^5.11.1, `hive_ce`/`hive_ce_flutter` ^2.22.0, `get_it` ^9.3.0, `fpdart` ^1.2.0, `freezed`/`freezed_annotation` ^4.0.3, `json_serializable` ^6.15.2, `build_runner` (latest compatible), `mocktail` ^1.0.5, `fl_chart` ^1.3.0, `local_auth` ^3.0.2, `flutter_secure_storage` ^11.2.0, `flutter_dotenv` ^6.0.1, `whisper_ggml` ^2.8.1.

## Epic List

### Epic 1: Foundation & Session Management

Users can create an account, log in, and have their session silently maintained or gracefully recovered; the app shell navigates between all four base surfaces with clear placeholders for what isn't built yet. Realizes UJ-2 (expired-session edge case). Delivered first (F000) — every later epic assumes this scaffold, the auth session lifecycle, and base navigation already exist. **No prior epic.**
**FRs covered:** FR-1, FR-2, FR-3

### Epic 2: Biometric Authentication Vault

Users unlock the app with Face ID/Touch ID (or PIN fallback) before any personal data is ever shown, with no lockout path and no biometric data ever leaving the device. Realizes UJ-1 (entry + edge case). Depends on Epic 1 — plugs the vault half into the single `go_router` redirect whose skeleton F000 already built (AD-14); this is a planned, non-competing extension of one shared file, not file churn.
**FRs covered:** FR-4, FR-5, FR-6, FR-7

### Epic 3: Multimodal Capture & Processing

Users can capture a journal Entry as text, voice, or photo — with audio transcribed on-device and photos OCR'd server-side before the Entry is ever persisted — and interrupting a capture never leaves a stray partial Entry behind. Realizes UJ-1. Depends on Epic 2 (the Insertion Modal is only reachable once the vault is unlocked). RF01 and RF02 stay merged because an un-transcribed audio Entry or un-OCR'd photo Entry is not a complete feature on its own (FR-9/FR-10 explicitly define the Entry as only "complete once processed") — unlike the Epic 4/5 split below, there is no standalone milestone at the RF01-only boundary. Introduces `features/entries/` (AD-6) as the shared port every later epic that creates or reads an Entry will consume.
**FRs covered:** FR-8, FR-9, FR-10, FR-11, FR-12, FR-13

### Epic 4: Timeline & History

Users can see every Entry they've ever captured, from any source, in one chronological view with a live per-entry sync status — and never lose track of something they wrote, even offline or mid-session-expiry. Realizes UJ-1 (as the destination for captured entries). Depends on Epic 3 (there's nothing to list until Entries exist). Kept separate from Epic 5: unlike RF01/RF02, a plain chronological timeline with working sync badges is a complete, independently demoable milestone with no search or filtering at all — splitting here, rather than merging, is the one place "same feature module" was not sufficient justification to combine two RF units.
**FRs covered:** FR-14, FR-15, FR-16, FR-17, FR-18

### Epic 5: Semantic Search & Filtering

Users can find any Entry again by meaning — not just exact keyword match — and narrow results by source and date range, with search debounced and filters clearing back to the full list without a reload. Realizes UJ-4. Depends on Epic 4 (search and filter operate over the timeline surface Epic 4 built). Extends the same `EntriesRepository` port (AD-6) with `list`/`search`, introducing no second Entry model — but is its own epic because it is its own user-facing milestone and its own journey (UJ-4), not a structural completion of Epic 4's job the way RF02 completes RF01's.

Users can have a persistent, multi-session conversation with an assistant that answers grounded in their own past Entries, turn their own reflective messages into real Entries with one tap, and occasionally receive an unprompted insight about a pattern in their writing — none of which ever blocks or corrupts the core chat experience when it fails.
