Users can request a narrative PDF + raw-data export for any date period, and always get their raw data even if the AI-generated narrative fails or the period turns out to be empty. Realizes UJ-5. Depends on Epic 4 (export operates over the same Entry history Timeline surfaces).
**FRs covered:** FR-34, FR-35, FR-36, FR-37

### Epic 8: Evolution Dashboard & Account Management

Users can see an on-demand chart of their journaling activity with an independent AI narrative, edit their display name, log out, and permanently delete their account and all associated data. Realizes UJ-6. Depends on Epic 1 (session/logout) and Epic 3 (dashboard aggregation needs Entries to aggregate, and recalculates whenever a new one is created).
**FRs covered:** FR-38, FR-39, FR-40, FR-41, FR-42, FR-43

## Epic 1: Foundation & Session Management

Users can create an account, log in, and have their session silently maintained or gracefully recovered; the app shell navigates between all four base surfaces with clear placeholders for what isn't built yet.

### Story 1.1: Project Scaffold, Stack Integration & Core Infrastructure

As a developer,
I want the Flutter project scaffolded with the pinned stack and the `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` integration verified working together in one bootstrap,
So that every feature built afterward has a stable, correctly-wired foundation instead of discovering an integration conflict mid-feature.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a fresh checkout of the repository
**When** `fvm flutter pub get` and the build runner are executed
**Then** the project resolves all pinned dependencies (Flutter 3.47.x family, `flutter_bloc` ^9.1.1, `go_router` ^18.1.1, `dio` ^5.11.1, `hive_ce`/`hive_ce_flutter` ^2.22.0, `get_it` ^9.3.0, `fpdart` ^1.2.0, `freezed`/`freezed_annotation` ^4.0.3, `json_serializable` ^6.15.2, `mocktail` ^1.0.5, `fl_chart` ^1.3.0, `local_auth` ^3.0.2, `flutter_secure_storage` ^11.2.0, `flutter_dotenv` ^6.0.1, `whisper_ggml` ^2.8.1) with no version conflicts.

**Given** the `lib/` directory after scaffolding
**When** inspected
**Then** it matches the Structural Seed exactly: `lib/core/{design_tokens.dart, network/, failure/, di/, cache/, resource.dart, isolated_side_effect.dart, session/}` and `lib/features/{auth, vault, entries, capture, chat, export, dashboard, account}/`, each pre-wired for the `data/domain/presentation` split.

**Given** a gitignored `.env` holding `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`
**When** the app boots
**Then** `flutter_dotenv` loads both values and no secret is hardcoded anywhere in source.

**Given** the DI bootstrap in `lib/core/di/`
**When** the app starts
**Then** exactly one `get_it` instance is registered, `dio` is configured through it, and an integration test proves `flutter_secure_storage` can be read/written through the same bootstrap — verifying the three packages work together before any feature is built on top of them.
**And** the sealed `Failure` hierarchy (AD-3, 14 subtypes) is defined in `lib/core/failure/`, the one retry interceptor (AD-4) retries only the 6 server `retryable:true` codes, and the one URL builder (AD-5) maps every operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>` with `apikey` sent on every call.
**And** one shared, table-driven `mocktail` test helper is built in `core/` that drives the 5-write-endpoint × 3-failure-type (timeout, malformed response, no connection) = 15-scenario matrix (RNF09) against a stubbed `ApiClient` — every later story that owns a write endpoint reuses this helper rather than building its own failure-matrix harness.

### Story 1.2: Design Token System & Core Component Library

As a developer,
I want the full visual token set and the generic button/text-field components implemented in `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` and a shared widgets layer,
So that every screen built afterward pulls its visual values and basic controls from one source, with zero hardcoded colors/fonts/spacing anywhere else in the app (RNF08).

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** `DESIGN.md`'s frontmatter token set (colors, typography, rounded, spacing)
**When** `design_tokens.dart` is implemented
**Then** every token name matches `DESIGN.md` verbatim (camelCase), and `elevation1`/`elevation2` are defined as literal shadow constants alongside it (UX-DR1).

**Given** the app's single supported configuration
**When** any screen renders
**Then** it is laid out for a fixed 390×844 logical-point portrait frame, light mode only — no breakpoint, landscape, or dark-mode code path exists anywhere (UX-DR35).

**Given** the primary, secondary, and text/ghost button components
**When** a button is disabled
**Then** it renders `colorBorder` background with `colorTextSecondary` text — never a dimmed opacity of its active state (UX-DR2).

**Given** the text-field component
**When** it is empty, focused, or holding a validation error
**Then** it shows the default, `colorPrimary`-at-1.5px-focused, and `colorError`-bordered states respectively, with no literal color/width defined outside `design_tokens.dart` (UX-DR3).
**And** every control built from these tokens honors Dynamic Type at every size without truncating or clipping (UX-DR22).

### Story 1.3: Account Creation and Login

As a new or returning user,
I want to create an account or log in with my email and password,
So that I can access my private journal.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the Entrar / Criar conta screen in login mode
**When** I submit a valid, registered email and password
**Then** `POST /auth/login` succeeds and I land on Home/Chat with a persisted session.

**Given** the same screen toggled to signup mode
**When** I submit an email and password
**Then** `POST /auth/signup` is called with exactly those two fields — no password-confirmation or display-name field exists anywhere on the screen (UX-DR31, resolves PRD OQ-2).

**Given** an invalid login attempt
**When** the backend returns `AUTH_INVALID`
**Then** the error shows inline under the fields using the text-field's error-border treatment, and the field is never cleared.

**Given** a malformed email
**When** I attempt to submit before any network call
**Then** client-side validation blocks the submit locally where possible, without a round trip.
**And** every call on this screen sends `apikey` plus `Authorization: Bearer <anon key>` per AD-5 — never a user token, since signup/login/refresh are the three `security: []` operations.

### Story 1.4: Silent Session Refresh & Persistence

As a returning user,
I want my session refreshed silently or remembered across app restarts,
So that I don't have to log in every time I open the app.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a previously authenticated session with a valid, unexpired token
**When** I restart the app
**Then** I land on Home/Chat without being re-prompted for credentials.

**Given** a session nearing or past expiry on app foreground
**When** the app checks session validity
**Then** it calls the session-check/refresh operation silently, with no visible loading UI unless the call exceeds the 300ms threshold (RNF01).
**And** exactly one `SessionStatus` stream is exposed from `features/auth/domain/` and registered once in DI as a singleton (AD-8) — no other code path re-derives session validity from a raw 401 or a second stream.

### Story 1.5: Expired-Session Recovery Overlay

As a user whose session has expired while using the app,
I want a "Sessão expirada" overlay that lets me re-authenticate without losing my place,
So that I never lose my context or feel like I'm starting over.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** I am on any screen and the backend reports `AUTH_EXPIRED`
**When** the overlay appears
**Then** it renders as a scrim over the current screen (confirmation-dialog component, neutral `colorTextPrimary` title, UX-DR16) — the screen underneath, including scroll position, is preserved, never navigated away from.

**Given** the overlay is visible
**When** I tap "Entrar novamente"
**Then** I am routed to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow (built in Epic 2) — never a full login form.

**Given** the overlay is open
**When** I try to interact with anything underneath the scrim
**Then** focus is trapped on the overlay until it is dismissed or actioned (UX-DR25).
**And** its entrance uses only the `scrimIn` (0.18s) choreography, and it is the only overlay permitted on screen at a time — it never stacks on top of another open overlay (UX-DR27, UX-DR36).

### Story 1.6: Base Navigation Shell with Feature Placeholders

As a user,
I want to navigate between Home/Chat, the side menu, Meus Registros, and Configurações from the moment I open the app,
So that the whole app feels complete and navigable even while individual features are still being built.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the app has launched
**When** I open the side menu (☰)
**Then** I can reach Chat Session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, and Planos de Ação — all four destinations resolve to a screen, none 404s or crashes.

**Given** a destination whose RF unit is not yet built
**When** I navigate to it
**Then** it renders a visually distinct, clearly-marked placeholder — never a screen that looks finished but does nothing.

**Given** the Planos de Ação placeholder (an explicit extension feature, never implemented per project policy)
**When** I open it
**Then** it is styled with full visual polish per the design tokens — never grayed-out or visibly "unfinished" (UX-DR32) — with no backend calls and no interactive drag/drop logic behind it.
**And** the side-menu avatar component (solid `colorPrimary` circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, 40px) is implemented here for reuse — not reimplementation — when Configurações needs its 52px variant later (UX-DR13).

## Epic 2: Biometric Authentication Vault

Users unlock the app with Face ID/Touch ID (or PIN fallback) before any personal data is ever shown, with no lockout path and no biometric data ever leaving the device.

### Story 2.1: Biometric/PIN App-Access Gate

As a user,
I want the app to require Face ID, Touch ID, or PIN before showing any of my data,
So that my journal stays private even if someone else picks up my phone.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the app is cold-started or resumed after the idle timeout
**When** the vault gate evaluates
**Then** no screen other than the vault/login screen is reachable until authentication succeeds.

**Given** the `go_router` redirect
**When** it evaluates on any navigation attempt
**Then** it composes exactly two gates in fixed order — `VaultStatus` first, then `SessionStatus` (AD-14) — and neither gate ever makes a network call to validate itself; biometric validation is 100% on-device, so no biometric data or call ever reaches the backend.

**Given** Face ID/Touch ID is available and enabled
**When** I open the app
**Then** the OS biometric prompt appears and, on success, routes me straight to Home/Chat.
**And** `features/vault/domain` exposes a `VaultStatus` stream the same way `features/auth/domain` exposes `SessionStatus` (AD-8 pattern), registered once in DI.

### Story 2.2: Biometric-Failure Fallback to PIN

As a user whose biometric check fails,
I want to fall back to entering a PIN,
So that I'm never locked out of my own journal.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** Face ID/Touch ID fails to recognize me
**When** the failure is reported
**Then** "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN" appears with a PIN entry path always reachable — never a dead end.

**Given** repeated biometric failures trigger an OS-level lockout
**When** that lockout is detected
**Then** the app routes to its own PIN fallback rather than retrying against the OS.

**Given** the PIN keypad (3×4 grid + backspace, progress dots, structural palette only, UX-DR14)
**When** I enter the 4th digit
**Then** the app auto-advances 350ms later with no explicit "confirm" tap (UX-DR27).
**And** the screen-reader announces the failure transition per the Accessibility Floor (UX-DR21), and the keypad's digits remain legible at the largest Dynamic Type size without truncation (UX-DR22).

### Story 2.3: Fixed 5-Minute Idle Re-Authentication Timeout

As a user,
I want re-authentication required only after 5 minutes backgrounded,
So that casual app-switching doesn't interrupt me but a forgotten unlocked phone stays protected.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the app is backgrounded for less than 5 minutes
**When** I resume it
**Then** no re-authentication is prompted.

**Given** the app is backgrounded for 5 minutes or more
**When** I resume it
**Then** re-authentication is always prompted, regardless of any user setting — this value is fixed, not user-configurable.
**And** this timeout is implemented as a fixed parameter within `features/vault/domain`, not as a shared `core/` constant, and is never re-tuned by any later story.

### Story 2.4: Biometric Preference Persistence

As a user,
I want to enable or disable the biometric gate from a setting that persists across restarts and reinstalls,
So that my preference travels with my account, not just my device.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** I toggle biometric gating on or off
**When** the toggle is changed
**Then** `PATCH /account/settings` persists the preference server-side, surfacing the Failure contract on error.

**Given** I disable biometrics
**When** I next open the app
**Then** PIN remains available as the access method — the vault itself can never be turned off entirely.

**Given** I reinstall the app or restart it after changing this setting elsewhere
**When** the app loads
**Then** the preference is fetched from the account, not read from a stale local-only cache.
**And** this story introduces a minimal Configurações screen (replacing Epic 1's placeholder) containing only this toggle — Epic 8 extends this same screen with profile editing, the dashboard, and account actions; it is never recreated from scratch.

## Epic 3: Multimodal Capture & Processing

Users can capture a journal Entry as text, voice, or photo — with audio transcribed on-device and photos OCR'd server-side before the Entry is ever persisted — and interrupting a capture never leaves a stray partial Entry behind.

### Story 3.1: Text Entry Capture & Insertion Modal Shell

As a user,
I want to open the "+" control and type free text to save as a journal Entry,
So that I can quickly capture what happened today in writing.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** I tap "+" on Home/Chat
**When** the Insertion Modal opens
**Then** it opens on the Texto tab by default with a three-segment tab bar (Texto/Áudio/Foto, UX-DR11) and all three tabs reset to idle/empty.

**Given** I type text and tap Salvar
**When** the save completes
**Then** `POST /entries` fires with `source=manual` and the modal closes, returning me to where I was.

**Given** `features/entries/` does not yet exist
**When** this story is built
**Then** it introduces `entries/domain` owning the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port (`create`), and the entries Hive box (AD-6) — this story is the first consumer of that port, never building its own local Entry model.

**Given** the device is offline
**When** I tap "+"
**Then** the entry point is disabled with the same offline-banner treatment as chat send (UX-DR30, AD-9) — there is no local-only queued write.
**And** interrupting before Salvar (closing the modal, switching tabs) never fires `POST /entries` (FR-11 — see Story 3.4 for the full cross-tab rule).

### Story 3.2: Audio Entry Capture & On-Device Transcription

As a user,
I want to record audio in the Insertion Modal and have it transcribed on-device,
So that I can speak my day instead of typing it, without my voice ever leaving my phone.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the Áudio tab
**When** I start recording
**Then** an animated waveform (UX-DR12) shows in the structural palette with a mono counter ticking up.

**Given** I stop recording
**When** `whisper_ggml` transcribes on-device
**Then** the waveform freezes at 35% opacity (UX-DR12) and exactly four states occur in sequence: recording → processing → transcribed → (on failure) error with retry — media is never discarded on failure.

**Given** transcription completes
**When** I review the text
**Then** it is editable before I tap Salvar, and the resulting Entry carries `source=audio`.

**Given** the audio file at any point in this pipeline
**When** any network call is inspected
**Then** no call ever contains audio bytes — transcription is 100% on-device (FR-12).
**And** the screen-reader announces each transition ("Gravando," "Transcrevendo," "Erro ao transcrever, toque para tentar novamente") per UX-DR21.

### Story 3.3: Photo Entry Capture & Backend OCR

As a user,
I want to capture or select a photo in the Insertion Modal and have its text recognized,
So that I can save a physical note or receipt-like artifact without retyping it.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the Foto tab
**When** I capture or select a photo
**Then** it is sent to `POST /media/ocr` to extract text before the Entry is created, mirroring the audio pipeline's four-state pattern (capture → processing OCR → recognized → error).

**Given** OCR fails with `OCR_NO_TEXT`
**When** the error state shows
**Then** it is presented as a distinct, non-retryable outcome with two recovery paths — "Tentar novamente" (re-invokes OCR on the same photo) and "Salvar só a foto" (saves the record with no extracted text) — never a single generic failure.

**Given** recognized text
**When** I review it
**Then** it is editable before I tap Salvar, and the resulting Entry carries `source=photo`.

**Given** the photo exceeds the upload size limit
**When** `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (413, non-retryable) is returned
**Then** a size-specific error message is shown with no retry button, since retrying the same oversized file cannot succeed.

### Story 3.4: Cancel-Safe Capture Across All Tabs

As a user,
I want interrupting a capture in progress to never create a partial Entry,
So that I never end up with junk in my journal from a capture I abandoned.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a recording or OCR/transcription in progress
**When** I switch to a different Insertion Modal tab
**Then** the in-flight capture is canceled outright — no partial Entry is created (resolves PRD OQ-3).

**Given** I back out of the modal mid-photo or stop a recording before tapping Salvar
**When** the modal closes
**Then** no `POST /entries` call fires for the abandoned capture.

**Given** any of the three tabs
**When** a capture is interrupted
**Then** it is the Insertion Modal's own internal tab state that resets — the three tabs remain internal states of one sheet, never nested sheets (UX-DR36).

## Epic 4: Timeline & History

Users can see every Entry they've ever captured, from any source, in one chronological view with a live per-entry sync status — and never lose track of something they wrote, even offline or mid-session-expiry.

### Story 4.1: Chronological Entry List with Origin Marking

As a user,
I want to see every Entry I've ever captured, from any source, in one chronological list grouped by date,
So that I never lose track of something I wrote.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** Entries from manual, audio, and photo sources
**When** Meus Registros loads
**Then** all Entries are listed together grouped by date, each visually marked with its origin via the record card's spine color (manual=`colorPrimary`, audio=olive green, photo=gray — chat=`colorAccent` reserved for Epic 6, UX-DR18).

**Given** the list is loading
**When** the `GET /entries` call takes longer than 300ms
**Then** skeleton rows show (UX-DR17); under 300ms, no loading UI appears at all (RNF01).

**Given** the session expires while I'm viewing this screen
**When** the FR-2 overlay (built in Epic 1) appears
**Then** it does so without crashing or losing my scroll position (FR-17).

**Given** the entries Hive box
**When** Entries are cached locally
**Then** it stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id — no local filtering, joining, or sorting of the cached collection (AD-15).
**And** no swipe gesture is ever implemented on a record card — Entries are immutable, so no gesture may imply an edit or delete that doesn't exist (UX-DR28).

### Story 4.2: Per-Entry Sync Badge

As a user,
I want to see at a glance whether each Entry has synced,
So that I know whether my capture is safely saved.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a freshly created Entry
**When** its write is in flight
**Then** its badge shows "Synchronizing" (ochre dot) until the server's write confirmation is reconciled, then flips to "Synchronized" (green dot).

**Given** a write fails (network or any Failure-contract code)
**When** the badge renders
**Then** it shows "Synchronization error" (red dot) until a subsequent successful write reconciles it.

**Given** the badge is in the error state
**When** I tap it
**Then** it retries that entry's write if the underlying code is retryable, or shows an inline explanation instead of a retry affordance if it is not (resolves PRD OQ-6).

**Given** one derivation function in `entries/domain`
**When** any screen renders a sync badge
**Then** it consumes that function's output, computed from `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and transient per-entry write state — no screen recomputes the badge inline (AD-10).
**And** the badge's dot color is always paired with an accessible label reachable on tap/long-focus, and its tappable retry area is ≥44pt even though the dot itself is small (UX-DR7, UX-DR23) — color never carries the state alone.
**And** the badge's update stream runs independently of the auth/session stream — a pending sync-badge transition is never blocked or cleared by session-expiry handling.

### Story 4.3: Empty-State Handling

As a user with no Entries yet,
I want a dedicated empty state instead of a blank list,
So that the app guides me back to capture rather than looking broken.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** zero Entries exist
**When** Meus Registros loads
**Then** a dedicated empty state renders — never a blank list.

**Given** the empty state
**When** I look for a way forward
**Then** it offers a path back to capture (a CTA that opens the Insertion Modal).

### Story 4.4: Entry Detail View

As a user,
I want to open a single Entry to see its full content,
So that I can review exactly what I wrote without any risk of accidentally changing it.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** an Entry in the list
**When** I open it
**Then** `GET /entries/:id` fetches and displays its full content with no edit affordance anywhere on the screen — Entries are immutable, and `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read only; no update/delete method is ever added (AD-11).

**Given** an Entry that doesn't exist or belongs to another user
**When** the detail request is made
**Then** the backend returns `NOT_FOUND`, never a permission-denied code, and the UI shows the same not-found treatment either way (RNF04).

**Given** this screen composes auth status, Sync Badge state, and Entry data
**When** those three streams are combined
**Then** they combine only through the domain layer — no BLoC in this feature imports another BLoC directly (AD-7, feature-specific NFR).

## Epic 5: Semantic Search & Filtering

Users can find any Entry again by meaning — not just exact keyword match — and narrow results by source and date range, with search debounced and filters clearing back to the full list without a reload.

### Story 5.1: Semantic Search with Debounced Input

As a user,
I want to search my Entries by meaning, not just exact words,
So that I can find things I wrote even if I phrased them differently.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** I type "ansiedade" into the search bar
**When** results return
**Then** they include an Entry that only used a related but different word (e.g., "nervosismo") because the match is semantic (`GET /entries/search`), not literal.

**Given** I am typing
**When** each keystroke lands
**Then** the request is debounced by 300ms before firing — no request fires on every keystroke.

**Given** the search bar component (UX-DR9)
**When** it renders
**Then** it is permanently docked at the top of Meus Registros with a trailing funnel icon and is never submitted with a button.

**Given** I am offline
**When** I attempt a semantic search
**Then** it resolves to `Failure.networkOffline` immediately — there is no client-side vector index to fall back to, so it is never served from cache, unlike plain entry reads (AD-9 search carve-out).

### Story 5.2: Metadata Filters

As a user,
I want to filter my Entries by source and date range,
So that I can narrow down to just the Entries I care about.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** no active search term
**When** I apply a source and/or date-range filter
**Then** `GET /entries` is queried with those filter parameters.

**Given** multiple active filters
**When** they combine
**Then** they use AND semantics — no tag/category filter exists, since categorization is an extension feature.

**Given** the filter chip component (UX-DR8) and filter sheet (UX-DR10)
**When** filters are active
**Then** chips render as removable, and the sheet itself is a `radiusLg`/`elevation2` bottom sheet with groups labeled in `textMonoCaption`.

### Story 5.3: Combined Search + Filter & Non-Disruptive Clearing

As a user,
I want my search term and my active filters to work together, and clearing them to feel instant,
So that filtering never feels like it's fighting my search.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** an active search term and active filters set simultaneously
**When** results are requested
**Then** `GET /entries/search` is queried carrying the same filter parameters, combined with AND logic (resolves PRD OQ-7, UX-DR29).

**Given** active filters
**When** I clear them
**Then** the full list is restored in place, without a full screen reload.

**Given** a reconnect after being offline
**When** the cache resyncs
**Then** it stays duplicate-free — no Entry appears twice because of a reconnect.

## Epic 6: Conversational Memory, Save-to-Journal & Insights

Users can have a persistent, multi-session conversation with an assistant that answers grounded in their own past Entries, turn their own reflective messages into real Entries with one tap, and occasionally receive an unprompted insight about a pattern in their writing — none of which ever blocks or corrupts the core chat experience when it fails.

### Story 6.1: Send Message & Receive RAG-Grounded Streaming Response

As a user,
I want to send a message to the assistant and get a response grounded in my own past Entries,
So that I feel genuinely understood rather than getting a generic reply.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** I type a message referencing something from weeks ago and send it
**When** the response streams in via SSE on `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`
**Then** it is grounded in semantic retrieval over my own Entries — not a stateless generic answer.

**Given** the response is streaming
**When** it renders
**Then** exactly three visible states exist: streaming/processing (progressively revealed text behind a blinking cursor, chat-bubble component UX-DR4), error, complete.

**Given** a Chat Message is sent
**When** it completes
**Then** it never automatically creates an Entry — RF10 (Story 6.4) is the sole, explicit exception.
**And** if Reduce Motion is enabled, the cursor-blink animation is skipped and the final text shows immediately instead (UX-DR24).

### Story 6.2: Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation

As a user,
I want to hold multiple named conversations and start a new one whenever I want a fresh start,
So that my chat history stays organized by topic or moment.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** I have existing Chat Sessions
**When** I open the side menu
**Then** they are listed and I can switch between them.

**Given** I tap "Novo Chat" from the side menu
**When** a new session starts
**Then** it opens empty with the composer focused and the placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem..." — no greeting copy invented beyond that.

**Given** I am offline
**When** I attempt to start a new Chat Session
**Then** `POST /chat/sessions` is blocked, consistent with the offline composer lock on existing conversations.
**And** a returning (not new) session restores the last conversation's scroll position when I open it.

### Story 6.3: Dropped-Stream Resilience & Offline Composer Lock

As a user,
I want a dropped response or an offline moment to never cost me my place in the conversation,
So that a flaky connection never feels like data loss.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a response stream drops mid-generation
**When** the failure is detected
**Then** the partial message stays on screen with a failure indicator (timestamp slot replaced by red retry copy, bubble content never cleared).

**Given** a dropped stream
**When** I tap retry
**Then** `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` regenerates the response without duplicating my original question.

23	
24	# Architecture Spine — Cerne
25	
26	## Design Paradigm
27	
28	**Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature, BLoC on top, errors carried as values.**
29	
30	- `presentation/` (BLoC/Cubit + widgets) → depends on → `domain/` (entities, use cases, repository/port interfaces) ← implemented by ← `data/` (DTOs, data sources, repository implementations).
31	- `domain/` is the only layer every other layer may depend on; it depends on nothing feature-specific and never on `package:flutter` (RNF06).
32	- Every operation that can fail (network, parse, local I/O) returns `Either<Failure, T>` (`fpdart`) at the repository boundary — no repository throws past itself (RNF09).
33	- `core/` sits beneath every feature and holds the only cross-feature-shared code: the `Failure` hierarchy, the API client/URL builder, the DI bootstrap, the local-cache boxes, `Resource<T>`, `isolatedSideEffect`, design tokens, and the `SessionStatus` contract.
34	
35	```mermaid
36	flowchart TD
37	    subgraph Feature["any lib/features/<name>/"]
38	        P["presentation (BLoC/Cubit, widgets)"]
39	        D["domain (entities, use cases, port interfaces)"]
40	        DA["data (DTOs, data sources, repository impl)"]
41	        P --> D
42	        DA --> D
43	    end
44	    Core["core/ (Failure, ApiClient, DI, cache, Resource<T>, SessionStatus, VaultStatus, design_tokens)"]
45	    D --> Core
46	    DA --> Core
47	    OtherDomain["another feature's domain/ (port interfaces only)"]
48	    P -.->|"AD-6: cross-feature calls only through the owning feature's domain port"| OtherDomain
49	```
50	
51	## Invariants & Rules
52	
53	### AD-1 — Layer dependency direction (RNF06)
54	
55	- **Binds:** all features
56	- **Prevents:** `domain/` depending on Flutter, on any `data/` (own or another feature's), or on another feature's `presentation/`.
57	- **Rule:** dependency direction is strictly `presentation → domain ← data`. `domain/` imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything under any `data/`. Only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins. `presentation/` never imports a feature's own or another feature's `data/` directly.
58	
59	### AD-2 — Either-everywhere error channel (RNF09)
60	
61	- **Binds:** all repositories (read and write)
62	- **Prevents:** a feature inventing its own error signaling (exceptions crossing the repository boundary, nullable returns, ad hoc string errors) that other code can't pattern-match generically.
63	- **Rule:** every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` for the chat SSE stream). `Failure` is the closed hierarchy in AD-3. No repository implementation lets a native/dio exception escape unmapped.
64	
65	### AD-3 — Closed `Failure` hierarchy `[ADOPTED]`
66	
67	- **Binds:** all
68	- **Prevents:** two features inventing different shapes for "network timeout," or silently dropping one of the server's 13 codes.
69	- **Rule:** one sealed `Failure` class in `core/`, exactly 14 subtypes — the 13 from `error-taxonomy.md` (`AuthExpired`, `AuthInvalid`, `NetworkTimeout`, `NetworkOffline`, `Validation`, `PiiCheckFailed`, `EmbeddingFailed`, `AiGenerationTimeout`, `NotFound`, `RateLimited`, `ExportEmptyPeriod`, `PayloadTooLarge`, `OcrNoText`) plus the local-only `MalformedResponse` (`retryable` hardcoded `false`, for the client's own parse-failure detection). Never redefined or subset per feature. `AuthInvalid` can only ever originate from `POST /auth/login` — no biometric/PIN check ever reaches the server (AD-14), so no feature maps a local vault failure to this code.
70	
71	### AD-4 — Retry policy lives in exactly one place `[ADOPTED]`
72	
73	- **Binds:** the API client
74	- **Prevents:** a feature writing its own retry loop that double-retries, or retries a `retryable:false` code.
75	- **Rule:** retry logic is implemented once (the `dio` interceptor / `ApiClient` wrapper), fires only for the 6 server `retryable:true` codes (`NETWORK_TIMEOUT`, `NETWORK_OFFLINE`, `PII_CHECK_FAILED`, `EMBEDDING_FAILED`, `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`, `RATE_LIMITED`). Every other code surfaces once, unretried.
76	
77	### AD-5 — Function-name URL construction and header policy
78	
79	- **Binds:** every network call
80	- **Prevents:** a feature string-concatenating the literal `openapi.yaml` REST path (which is not a real URL) or re-deciding which `Authorization` value to send.
81	- **Rule:** one URL builder in `core/` maps each operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>`. One `dio` interceptor owns headers: `apikey` on every call; `Authorization: Bearer <anon key>` only on the three `security: []` operations (signup, login, refresh); `Authorization: Bearer <user token>` on every other (`bearerAuth`) operation.
82	
83	### AD-6 — `entries` owns `Entry` from RF01 onward; every other feature reaches it only through a domain-layer port
84	
85	- **Binds:** RF01 (capture → entries, the *first* consumer — delivery order builds RF01 three units before RF06/RF07), RF10 (chat → entries), and any future cross-feature dependency
86	- **Prevents:** (a) RF01 inventing its own local `Entry` model/repository/cache box because `features/entries/` "doesn't exist yet" at its position in the delivery order, which RF06/RF07 would then duplicate; (b) any feature reaching into `entries`'s `data/`, repository, data source, or BLoC — the exact violation RF10's acceptance criteria calls out, which would also break RNF06.
87	- **Rule:** `features/entries/` is scaffolded at RF01 (not RF06/RF07) because RF01 is the first unit that must call `POST /entries` (requirements.md §6.2). From RF01 on, `entries/domain` owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port (`create`, `read` — see AD-11), and the entries Hive box. `entries` exposes an abstract `CreateEntryUseCase`/`SaveEntryUseCase`-shaped port; RF01's `capture` feature and RF10's `chat` feature are both *consumers* — each only ever imports and injects that abstract type from `entries/domain`, never anything from `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/`. RF06/RF07 extend the same `EntriesRepository` port with `list`/`search` methods; they do not introduce a second entry model or a second owner. The port's `create` is idempotent on `(origin, chatMessageId)`: a second call for a `chatMessageId` that already has an entry never creates a duplicate — the implementation (not the port's type signature) is responsible for this check, binding on RF10's build.
88	
89	### AD-7 — No BLoC-to-BLoC references
90	
91	- **Binds:** all (generalizes RF07's explicit AC to every feature)
92	- **Prevents:** hidden coupling and circular-rebuild chains between presentation units built independently.
93	- **Rule:** a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency, same-feature or cross-feature. Composition of multiple independent state sources happens by injecting the underlying `domain/` streams/use-cases into each BLoC independently, or via `BlocListener`/`MultiBlocListener` in the widget tree — never a direct BLoC → BLoC reference.
94	
95	### AD-8 — Single `SessionStatus` source of truth
96	
97	- **Binds:** F000 (go_router redirect), RF07 (composite auth × sync × data state), any feature that needs session validity
98	- **Prevents:** two independently-built screens disagreeing on what "session expired" means or when to prompt re-login.
99	- **Rule:** exactly one `SessionStatus` stream, exposed from the auth feature's `domain/`, registered once in DI as a singleton. Every consumer injects/listens to that stream; none re-derives session state from a raw 401, from its own `GET /auth/session` poll, or from a second stream. `SessionStatus` governs *server session validity only* — it composes with the local vault gate per AD-14, it does not replace it.
100	
101	### AD-9 — Cloud-only: no offline write queue
102	
103	- **Binds:** all repositories (generalizes RF06's "cloud-only" note and RF04's "blocked offline" writes)
104	- **Prevents:** a feature building a local write-queue/outbox that silently diverges from "offline permits viewing cached data only."
105	- **Rule:** a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)` — it is never queued for later. Plain reads (`GET /entries`, `GET /chat/sessions`, `GET .../messages`) transparently fall back to the local `hive_ce` cache. **Semantic search is the one read exception:** `GET /entries/search` has no client-side vector index to fall back to, so with no connectivity it also resolves to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)`, same as a write — it is never served from cache. The only client-side "pending write" state is transient, in-memory, scoped to one in-flight request (it feeds AD-10's `Synchronizing` badge state) — it is never persisted as a queue.
106	
107	### AD-10 — Sync badge is a pure client-side derivation (locks `sync-badge.md`)
108	
109	- **Binds:** every screen that renders the per-entry sync badge (chat save confirmation, My Records list, any future one)
110	- **Prevents:** two screens computing `Synchronizing`/`Error`/`Synchronized` differently.
111	- **Rule:** one derivation function lives in `entries/domain`, computed from three inputs: `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and the transient per-entry write state (AD-9) — which is itself one of three values: no pending write (→ `Synchronized`), a write in flight (→ `Synchronizing`), or the in-flight write's `Future` resolved to `Left(Failure)` (→ `Synchronization error`, held until the next write attempt reconciles it). Every screen consumes that function's output; none recomputes the badge inline. The server never supplies a `sync_status` field — `requirements.md` §8 is wrong on this point (`sync-badge.md` and the `Entry` schema win).
112	
113	### AD-11 — Entry immutability
114	
115	- **Binds:** the entries feature
116	- **Prevents:** a unit speculatively adding an update/delete path the backend doesn't support.
117	- **Rule:** `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read operations only. No update or delete method is ever added, matching the backend's lack of `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`.
118	
119	### AD-12 — Shared view-state scoped to single-source-of-truth fetches `[ADOPTED]`
120	
121	- **Binds:** RF06 (search results), RF09 (dashboard aggregate/narrative) — explicitly *not* RF02, RF04, or RF07
122	- **Prevents:** forcing a composite or multi-stage state machine into a generic fetch enum, and the reverse: ad hoc one-off state shapes where a shared one would do.
123	- **Rule:** generic `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) lives in `core/`, used only by screens with one data source and one fetch lifecycle. RF02's capture pipeline (`recording`/`processing`/`transcribed`/`error`), RF07's composite auth × sync × data state, and RF04's chat message stream (append-only, streaming/SSE, not a single fetch) each define their own sealed state class — never forced into `Resource<T>`. RF08's proactive-insight overlay is a value appended onto RF04's existing chat state, not a parallel `Resource<T>`.
124	
125	### AD-13 — `isolatedSideEffect` contract fixed now, implementation deferred `[ADOPTED]`
126	
127	- **Binds:** RF08, RF10 (both state the identical failure-isolation requirement)
128	- **Prevents:** RF08 reinventing its own failure-isolation wrapper (or importing RF10's feature-local one), producing two incompatible "never block the caller on failure" implementations.
129	- **Rule:** `core/` holds a never-throws helper with signature `Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped (never throws past itself); it ships with RF10, delivery order's first consumer (RF04 → RF10 → RF08), not built speculatively in F000. The helper's own `Future` always completes independently of the caller: RF10 may `await` it before updating its button state, and RF08 must be able to call it **without** awaiting (fire-and-forget) so a slow/failed insight generation never blocks or delays the chat stream. RF08 reuses it from `core/` without a cross-feature import.
130	
131	### AD-14 — One `go_router` redirect composes exactly two gates, in a fixed order: vault, then session
132	
133	- **Binds:** F000 (builds the redirect skeleton + `SessionStatus` half), RF03 (plugs the vault half into the same redirect)
134	- **Prevents:** F000 and RF03 each building an independent navigation gate (two competing `redirect` callbacks, or RF03 bolting a second check onto screens individually) — `go_router` supports only one top-level `redirect`, so two independently-built gates cannot both "just work."
135	- **Rule:** the redirect composes exactly two domain-level streams, evaluated in this order: (1) `VaultStatus` (local-only — biometric/PIN unlocked, Face-ID-failed-offer-PIN, or locked after the 5-minute background timeout; RF03 exposes it from `features/vault/domain` the same way auth exposes `SessionStatus`, AD-8) — checked *first*, before any network state, because it gates whether the app may show anything at all; then (2) `SessionStatus` (AD-8) once the vault is unlocked. Neither gate ever reaches the server to validate itself (`POST /auth/login` is the only path that can produce `AuthInvalid`, per AD-3) — the vault is validated entirely on-device, consistent with the backend having no biometric-unlock endpoint.
136	
137	### AD-15 — The local cache is a projection, never a query engine
138	
139	- **Binds:** `entries`, `chat` — every feature with a `hive_ce` box `[ADOPTED, promoted from the F000 forge session]`
140	- **Prevents:** a unit adding local filtering, joining, or sorting logic "for performance" or "for offline support," which would then disagree with the server's own filter semantics (AD-9's offline read rule assumes the cache's content is a verbatim copy, not a re-derived view).
141	- **Rule:** every query dimension (`source`, `dateFrom`/`dateTo`, semantic search, pagination cursor) is a server-side query parameter per `openapi.yaml`. A `hive_ce` box stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id (or by session id for messages); no feature ever filters, joins, sorts, or re-derives a different view from a cached collection — a cache miss or a dimension not covered by AD-9's offline-read rule surfaces `Failure.networkOffline`, it is never approximated locally.
142	
143	## Consistency Conventions
144	
145	| Concern | Convention |
146	| --- | --- |
147	| Feature naming | `lib/features/<feature>/` one of: `auth`, `vault`, `capture`, `entries`, `chat`, `export`, `dashboard`, `account` — see Capability → Architecture Map |
148	| Errors | `Failure` sealed hierarchy (AD-3) everywhere; UI maps a `Failure` to copy using its `retryable` flag, never a hardcoded per-screen message list |
149	| IDs & dates | server-assigned string IDs and ISO-8601 timestamps passed through verbatim from DTOs (`freezed`+`json_serializable`); the client never generates or reformats an entity ID |
150	| Visual values | `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` only (RNF08) — no color/font/spacing/radius literal anywhere else |
151	| Network envelope | one `ApiClient`/URL-builder + one header interceptor (AD-5); no feature constructs a request URL or header set itself |
152	| State composition | `Resource<T>` for single-source fetches (AD-12); no BLoC-to-BLoC references (AD-7) |
153	| Testing | `mocktail` stubs one `ApiClient` interface per repository test, not a fake transport layer; one shared table-driven helper drives the 5-write-endpoints × 3-failure-types = 15-scenario matrix (RNF09); ≥80% line coverage gate on every `domain/` (RNF07) |
154	| Config/secrets | `.env` (`FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) loaded via `flutter_dotenv` `[ASSUMPTION — settled here; requirements.md left it "free," no prior session decided it]`; never committed, never hardcoded |
155	| AI provider access | the app never calls Claude or Voyage AI directly — every AI-backed feature goes through the backend's documented endpoints (project policy, binding on all features) |
156	| Local cache | `hive_ce` boxes are a projection of server responses, never a query engine (AD-15) |
157	| Pagination/cursor | every paginated list (`entries`, `entries/search`, `chat_sessions`, `chat_messages`) uses the server's own cursor convention verbatim; the cursor string is cached alongside the box it pages (AD-15) — `entries` and `entries/search` share one cursor convention since both live in the one `entries` feature (AD-6) |
158	| Fixed numeric parameters (`requirements.md` §10 — not reinterpretable) | background session timeout 5 min (RF03) · search debounce 300 ms (RF06) · proactive-insight trigger N=5 user messages OR T=2 min inactivity, fires once per satisfied condition (RF08) · dashboard rendering scenarios 0 / 1 / >30 entries (RF09) · local UI latency <100 ms, loading indicator threshold >300 ms (RNF01) · domain coverage ≥80% (RNF07) · 5 write endpoints × 3 failure types = 15 scenarios (RNF09) — each is implemented inside its owning feature (not a shared core constant), but none may be approximated or re-tuned by whichever unit builds it |
159	
160	## Stack

184

227	## Capability → Architecture Map
228	
229	| Capability / Area | Lives in | Governed by |
230	| --- | --- | --- |
231	| F000 — scaffold, tokens, HTTP client, auth, base nav | `core/`, `features/auth/` | AD-1..AD-5, AD-8, AD-14 (session half) |
232	| RF03 — biometric/PIN vault | `features/vault/` | AD-14 (vault half), AD-3 (`AuthInvalid` note) |
233	| RF01 — multimodal capture | `features/capture/` → `features/entries/` (introduces it) | AD-1, AD-2, AD-6, AD-9, AD-15 |
234	| RF02 — STT/OCR processing | `features/capture/` | AD-12 (excluded — own state machine) |
235	| RF07 — multi-source history (timeline) | `features/entries/` (extends with timeline read) | AD-7, AD-8, AD-10, AD-12 (excluded), AD-15 |
236	| RF06 — semantic search/filter | `features/entries/` (extends with search) | AD-9 (search carve-out), AD-12, AD-15 |
237	| RF04 — chat with memory (RAG) | `features/chat/` | AD-1, AD-2, AD-9, AD-12 (own stream, excluded) |
238	| RF10 — save chat message as entry | `features/chat/` → `features/entries/` | AD-6 (idempotency), AD-13 |
239	| RF08 — proactive insights | `features/chat/` | AD-12 (overlay on chat state), AD-13 (fire-and-forget) |
240	| RF05 — personal summary export | `features/export/` | AD-1, AD-2 |
241	| RF09 — temporal summaries/dashboard | `features/dashboard/` | AD-12 |

244	## Deferred
245	
246	- **Epic/story breakdown within each build unit** — this spine fixes cross-unit invariants, not per-story task sequencing; owned by `bmad-create-epics-and-stories`.
247	- **CI/CD pipeline and release process** — no CI tool, test-runner wiring, or App Store distribution step is specified anywhere in the input package, and no project deadline is stated (flagged as an open PRD question). Revisit once a submission/demo deadline exists.
248	- **Exact fvm-pinned Flutter/Dart patch and the real `flutter test`/`flutter analyze` invocations** — `AGENTS.md`'s "Running and verifying" section leaves these open until F000 scaffolds the project; this spine names the current stable family (3.47.x), not a committed patch.
249	- **Persona system-prompt wiring and manual-tag UI behavior** — both are explicit extension features (`requirements.md` §2) that receive no functional implementation; no architecture owns their logic.
250	- **Dashboard cache-invalidation behavior (RF09 AC)** — a presentation-layer concern for whichever unit builds RF09, not a local-cache architecture decision.
251	- **Combined search + filter interaction semantics** when both a search term and date/source filters are active — flagged as an open PRD question (blocks RF06); `requirements.md` §6 fixes AND-logic between two *filters*, but search-term-plus-filter combination is still open. Resolve at RF06 build time, not here.
252	- **Product-level open questions carried from the PRD, not resolved here because they're not architecture-level:** signup field set (password confirmation / display name — blocks F000), tab-switching mid-capture in the Insertion Modal (discard/warn/persist — blocks RF01), whether the sync-badge error state needs a visible retry affordance or reconciliation-on-next-write is sufficient (blocks RF07). None of the three changes an AD in this spine regardless of how they're answered; each is a product decision for the unit that builds it.
253	- **Integration spike flagged, not yet run:** `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` have not been verified working together in one scaffold (each is independently current per the Stack table, but their combination at F000's bootstrap time is unverified). Run this as the first thing F000 does, before building on top of it.

# Architecture Spine — Cerne

## Design Paradigm

**Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature, BLoC on top, errors carried as values.**

- `presentation/` (BLoC/Cubit + widgets) → depends on → `domain/` (entities, use cases, repository/port interfaces) ← implemented by ← `data/` (DTOs, data sources, repository implementations).
- `domain/` is the only layer every other layer may depend on; it depends on nothing feature-specific and never on `package:flutter` (RNF06).
- Every operation that can fail (network, parse, local I/O) returns `Either<Failure, T>` (`fpdart`) at the repository boundary — no repository throws past itself (RNF09).
- `core/` sits beneath every feature and holds the only cross-feature-shared code: the `Failure` hierarchy, the API client/URL builder, the DI bootstrap, the local-cache boxes, `Resource<T>`, `isolatedSideEffect`, design tokens, and the `SessionStatus` contract.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Feature["any lib/features/<name>/"]
        P["presentation (BLoC/Cubit, widgets)"]
        D["domain (entities, use cases, port interfaces)"]
        DA["data (DTOs, data sources, repository impl)"]
        P --> D
        DA --> D
    end
    Core["core/ (Failure, ApiClient, DI, cache, Resource<T>, SessionStatus, VaultStatus, design_tokens)"]
    D --> Core
    DA --> Core
    OtherDomain["another feature's domain/ (port interfaces only)"]
    P -.->|"AD-6: cross-feature calls only through the owning feature's domain port"| OtherDomain
```

## Invariants & Rules

### AD-1 — Layer dependency direction (RNF06)

- **Binds:** all features
- **Prevents:** `domain/` depending on Flutter, on any `data/` (own or another feature's), or on another feature's `presentation/`.
- **Rule:** dependency direction is strictly `presentation → domain ← data`. `domain/` imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything under any `data/`. Only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins. `presentation/` never imports a feature's own or another feature's `data/` directly.

### AD-2 — Either-everywhere error channel (RNF09)

- **Binds:** all repositories (read and write)
- **Prevents:** a feature inventing its own error signaling (exceptions crossing the repository boundary, nullable returns, ad hoc string errors) that other code can't pattern-match generically.
- **Rule:** every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` for the chat SSE stream). `Failure` is the closed hierarchy in AD-3. No repository implementation lets a native/dio exception escape unmapped.

### AD-3 — Closed `Failure` hierarchy `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** all
- **Prevents:** two features inventing different shapes for "network timeout," or silently dropping one of the server's 13 codes.
- **Rule:** one sealed `Failure` class in `core/`, exactly 14 subtypes — the 13 from `error-taxonomy.md` (`AuthExpired`, `AuthInvalid`, `NetworkTimeout`, `NetworkOffline`, `Validation`, `PiiCheckFailed`, `EmbeddingFailed`, `AiGenerationTimeout`, `NotFound`, `RateLimited`, `ExportEmptyPeriod`, `PayloadTooLarge`, `OcrNoText`) plus the local-only `MalformedResponse` (`retryable` hardcoded `false`, for the client's own parse-failure detection). Never redefined or subset per feature. `AuthInvalid` can only ever originate from `POST /auth/login` — no biometric/PIN check ever reaches the server (AD-14), so no feature maps a local vault failure to this code.

### AD-4 — Retry policy lives in exactly one place `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** the API client
- **Prevents:** a feature writing its own retry loop that double-retries, or retries a `retryable:false` code.
- **Rule:** retry logic is implemented once (the `dio` interceptor / `ApiClient` wrapper), fires only for the 6 server `retryable:true` codes (`NETWORK_TIMEOUT`, `NETWORK_OFFLINE`, `PII_CHECK_FAILED`, `EMBEDDING_FAILED`, `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`, `RATE_LIMITED`). Every other code surfaces once, unretried.

### AD-5 — Function-name URL construction and header policy

- **Binds:** every network call
- **Prevents:** a feature string-concatenating the literal `openapi.yaml` REST path (which is not a real URL) or re-deciding which `Authorization` value to send.
- **Rule:** one URL builder in `core/` maps each operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>`. One `dio` interceptor owns headers: `apikey` on every call; `Authorization: Bearer <anon key>` only on the three `security: []` operations (signup, login, refresh); `Authorization: Bearer <user token>` on every other (`bearerAuth`) operation.

### AD-6 — `entries` owns `Entry` from RF01 onward; every other feature reaches it only through a domain-layer port

- **Binds:** RF01 (capture → entries, the *first* consumer — delivery order builds RF01 three units before RF06/RF07), RF10 (chat → entries), and any future cross-feature dependency
- **Prevents:** (a) RF01 inventing its own local `Entry` model/repository/cache box because `features/entries/` "doesn't exist yet" at its position in the delivery order, which RF06/RF07 would then duplicate; (b) any feature reaching into `entries`'s `data/`, repository, data source, or BLoC — the exact violation RF10's acceptance criteria calls out, which would also break RNF06.
- **Rule:** `features/entries/` is scaffolded at RF01 (not RF06/RF07) because RF01 is the first unit that must call `POST /entries` (requirements.md §6.2). From RF01 on, `entries/domain` owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port (`create`, `read` — see AD-11), and the entries Hive box. `entries` exposes an abstract `CreateEntryUseCase`/`SaveEntryUseCase`-shaped port; RF01's `capture` feature and RF10's `chat` feature are both *consumers* — each only ever imports and injects that abstract type from `entries/domain`, never anything from `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/`. RF06/RF07 extend the same `EntriesRepository` port with `list`/`search` methods; they do not introduce a second entry model or a second owner. The port's `create` is idempotent on `(origin, chatMessageId)`: a second call for a `chatMessageId` that already has an entry never creates a duplicate — the implementation (not the port's type signature) is responsible for this check, binding on RF10's build.

### AD-7 — No BLoC-to-BLoC references

- **Binds:** all (generalizes RF07's explicit AC to every feature)
- **Prevents:** hidden coupling and circular-rebuild chains between presentation units built independently.
- **Rule:** a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency, same-feature or cross-feature. Composition of multiple independent state sources happens by injecting the underlying `domain/` streams/use-cases into each BLoC independently, or via `BlocListener`/`MultiBlocListener` in the widget tree — never a direct BLoC → BLoC reference.

### AD-8 — Single `SessionStatus` source of truth

- **Binds:** F000 (go_router redirect), RF07 (composite auth × sync × data state), any feature that needs session validity
- **Prevents:** two independently-built screens disagreeing on what "session expired" means or when to prompt re-login.
- **Rule:** exactly one `SessionStatus` stream, exposed from the auth feature's `domain/`, registered once in DI as a singleton. Every consumer injects/listens to that stream; none re-derives session state from a raw 401, from its own `GET /auth/session` poll, or from a second stream. `SessionStatus` governs *server session validity only* — it composes with the local vault gate per AD-14, it does not replace it.

### AD-9 — Cloud-only: no offline write queue

- **Binds:** all repositories (generalizes RF06's "cloud-only" note and RF04's "blocked offline" writes)
- **Prevents:** a feature building a local write-queue/outbox that silently diverges from "offline permits viewing cached data only."
- **Rule:** a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)` — it is never queued for later. Plain reads (`GET /entries`, `GET /chat/sessions`, `GET .../messages`) transparently fall back to the local `hive_ce` cache. **Semantic search is the one read exception:** `GET /entries/search` has no client-side vector index to fall back to, so with no connectivity it also resolves to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)`, same as a write — it is never served from cache. The only client-side "pending write" state is transient, in-memory, scoped to one in-flight request (it feeds AD-10's `Synchronizing` badge state) — it is never persisted as a queue.

### AD-10 — Sync badge is a pure client-side derivation (locks `sync-badge.md`)

- **Binds:** every screen that renders the per-entry sync badge (chat save confirmation, My Records list, any future one)
- **Prevents:** two screens computing `Synchronizing`/`Error`/`Synchronized` differently.
- **Rule:** one derivation function lives in `entries/domain`, computed from three inputs: `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and the transient per-entry write state (AD-9) — which is itself one of three values: no pending write (→ `Synchronized`), a write in flight (→ `Synchronizing`), or the in-flight write's `Future` resolved to `Left(Failure)` (→ `Synchronization error`, held until the next write attempt reconciles it). Every screen consumes that function's output; none recomputes the badge inline. The server never supplies a `sync_status` field — `requirements.md` §8 is wrong on this point (`sync-badge.md` and the `Entry` schema win).

### AD-11 — Entry immutability

- **Binds:** the entries feature
- **Prevents:** a unit speculatively adding an update/delete path the backend doesn't support.
- **Rule:** `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read operations only. No update or delete method is ever added, matching the backend's lack of `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`.

### AD-12 — Shared view-state scoped to single-source-of-truth fetches `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** RF06 (search results), RF09 (dashboard aggregate/narrative) — explicitly *not* RF02, RF04, or RF07
- **Prevents:** forcing a composite or multi-stage state machine into a generic fetch enum, and the reverse: ad hoc one-off state shapes where a shared one would do.
- **Rule:** generic `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) lives in `core/`, used only by screens with one data source and one fetch lifecycle. RF02's capture pipeline (`recording`/`processing`/`transcribed`/`error`), RF07's composite auth × sync × data state, and RF04's chat message stream (append-only, streaming/SSE, not a single fetch) each define their own sealed state class — never forced into `Resource<T>`. RF08's proactive-insight overlay is a value appended onto RF04's existing chat state, not a parallel `Resource<T>`.

### AD-13 — `isolatedSideEffect` contract fixed now, implementation deferred `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** RF08, RF10 (both state the identical failure-isolation requirement)
- **Prevents:** RF08 reinventing its own failure-isolation wrapper (or importing RF10's feature-local one), producing two incompatible "never block the caller on failure" implementations.
- **Rule:** `core/` holds a never-throws helper with signature `Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped (never throws past itself); it ships with RF10, delivery order's first consumer (RF04 → RF10 → RF08), not built speculatively in F000. The helper's own `Future` always completes independently of the caller: RF10 may `await` it before updating its button state, and RF08 must be able to call it **without** awaiting (fire-and-forget) so a slow/failed insight generation never blocks or delays the chat stream. RF08 reuses it from `core/` without a cross-feature import.

### AD-14 — One `go_router` redirect composes exactly two gates, in a fixed order: vault, then session

- **Binds:** F000 (builds the redirect skeleton + `SessionStatus` half), RF03 (plugs the vault half into the same redirect)
- **Prevents:** F000 and RF03 each building an independent navigation gate (two competing `redirect` callbacks, or RF03 bolting a second check onto screens individually) — `go_router` supports only one top-level `redirect`, so two independently-built gates cannot both "just work."
- **Rule:** the redirect composes exactly two domain-level streams, evaluated in this order: (1) `VaultStatus` (local-only — biometric/PIN unlocked, Face-ID-failed-offer-PIN, or locked after the 5-minute background timeout; RF03 exposes it from `features/vault/domain` the same way auth exposes `SessionStatus`, AD-8) — checked *first*, before any network state, because it gates whether the app may show anything at all; then (2) `SessionStatus` (AD-8) once the vault is unlocked. Neither gate ever reaches the server to validate itself (`POST /auth/login` is the only path that can produce `AuthInvalid`, per AD-3) — the vault is validated entirely on-device, consistent with the backend having no biometric-unlock endpoint.

### AD-15 — The local cache is a projection, never a query engine

- **Binds:** `entries`, `chat` — every feature with a `hive_ce` box `[ADOPTED, promoted from the F000 forge session]`
- **Prevents:** a unit adding local filtering, joining, or sorting logic "for performance" or "for offline support," which would then disagree with the server's own filter semantics (AD-9's offline read rule assumes the cache's content is a verbatim copy, not a re-derived view).
- **Rule:** every query dimension (`source`, `dateFrom`/`dateTo`, semantic search, pagination cursor) is a server-side query parameter per `openapi.yaml`. A `hive_ce` box stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id (or by session id for messages); no feature ever filters, joins, sorts, or re-derives a different view from a cached collection — a cache miss or a dimension not covered by AD-9's offline-read rule surfaces `Failure.networkOffline`, it is never approximated locally.

## Consistency Conventions

| Concern | Convention |
| --- | --- |
| Feature naming | `lib/features/<feature>/` one of: `auth`, `vault`, `capture`, `entries`, `chat`, `export`, `dashboard`, `account` — see Capability → Architecture Map |
| Errors | `Failure` sealed hierarchy (AD-3) everywhere; UI maps a `Failure` to copy using its `retryable` flag, never a hardcoded per-screen message list |
| IDs & dates | server-assigned string IDs and ISO-8601 timestamps passed through verbatim from DTOs (`freezed`+`json_serializable`); the client never generates or reformats an entity ID |
| Visual values | `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` only (RNF08) — no color/font/spacing/radius literal anywhere else |
| Network envelope | one `ApiClient`/URL-builder + one header interceptor (AD-5); no feature constructs a request URL or header set itself |
| State composition | `Resource<T>` for single-source fetches (AD-12); no BLoC-to-BLoC references (AD-7) |
| Testing | `mocktail` stubs one `ApiClient` interface per repository test, not a fake transport layer; one shared table-driven helper drives the 5-write-endpoints × 3-failure-types = 15-scenario matrix (RNF09); ≥80% line coverage gate on every `domain/` (RNF07) |
| Config/secrets | `.env` (`FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) loaded via `flutter_dotenv` `[ASSUMPTION — settled here; requirements.md left it "free," no prior session decided it]`; never committed, never hardcoded |
| AI provider access | the app never calls Claude or Voyage AI directly — every AI-backed feature goes through the backend's documented endpoints (project policy, binding on all features) |
| Local cache | `hive_ce` boxes are a projection of server responses, never a query engine (AD-15) |
| Pagination/cursor | every paginated list (`entries`, `entries/search`, `chat_sessions`, `chat_messages`) uses the server's own cursor convention verbatim; the cursor string is cached alongside the box it pages (AD-15) — `entries` and `entries/search` share one cursor convention since both live in the one `entries` feature (AD-6) |
| Fixed numeric parameters (`requirements.md` §10 — not reinterpretable) | background session timeout 5 min (RF03) · search debounce 300 ms (RF06) · proactive-insight trigger N=5 user messages OR T=2 min inactivity, fires once per satisfied condition (RF08) · dashboard rendering scenarios 0 / 1 / >30 entries (RF09) · local UI latency <100 ms, loading indicator threshold >300 ms (RNF01) · domain coverage ≥80% (RNF07) · 5 write endpoints × 3 failure types = 15 scenarios (RNF09) — each is implemented inside its owning feature (not a shared core constant), but none may be approximated or re-tuned by whichever unit builds it |

# Generate Tracking

Discovery is your call; everything after it is the script's.

1. Identify the epic files. The gate inventory already surfaced them — typically `epics.md`, `epic-*.md`, or a sharded `epics/` folder in `{planning_artifacts}`, but trust content over filename. If both a whole document and a sharded version exist, ask which is current rather than guessing.
2. Run the script, passing every epic file:

   ```
   uv run {skill-root}/scripts/sprint_plan.py generate \
     --epic-file <path> [--epic-file <path> ...] \
     --status-file {implementation_artifacts}/sprint-status.yaml \
     --stories-dir {implementation_artifacts} \
     --project "{project_name}" --date "{date}"
   ```

   `{date}` must be `MM-DD-YYYY HH:MM` — the format the staleness check parses. The script owns parsing (`## Epic N:` / `### Story N.M: Title` → kebab-case keys; fenced code blocks ignored), ordering (epic, its stories, its retrospective), merging with any existing file (preserve advanced statuses, never downgrade; legacy v6 values like `drafted`/`contexted` are normalized to their modern meaning, never reset; `action_items`, custom keys, and user comments carried through; `project_key`/`tracking_system`/`story_location` kept from the existing file unless overridden by flag), story-file detection (a story file on disk floors its status at `ready-for-dev`), atomic writes, and post-write validation. It prints a JSON report. Add `--dry-run` to preview — the report's `in_sync`, `new_entries`, `dropped_orphans`, `illegal`, and `legacy_mapped` fields answer "is tracking in sync?" without writing.

3. Read the JSON report and act on it — this is where judgment re-enters:
   - `warnings` about unparsed Epic/Story-like headings mean the epic file deviates from the standard format. Show the user, fix the headings together (or accept the omission), and rerun.
   - `dropped_orphans` are entries that existed in the old status file but match nothing in the epics — usually renames. Each carries its old status; reconcile with the user, then transplant by rerunning with `--set <new-key>=<old-status>`.
   - If the epics defeat the parser entirely (a format the regexes can't see), fall back to building the file yourself against `sprint-status-template.yaml`, and tell the user the deterministic path didn't apply.
